claims.statement: Aderyn y Corff (Aderyn corff, Deryn corff, Aderyn y Corph; corpse bird), a bird of Welsh folklore that portends death.
claims.statement_id: Aderyn y Corff (Aderyn corff, Deryn corff, Aderyn y Corph; burung mayat), burung folklor Welsh (Wales), pertanda kematian.
claims.quote: is a bird from Welsh folklore who portends death.

claims.statement: Chirps at a dying person's door, like dewch (come); no feathers or wings; lives on another plane.
claims.statement_id: Berkicau di pintu orang yang akan meninggal, mirip dewch (datanglah); tanpa bulu dan sayap; hidup di alam lain.
claims.quote: It is said to chirp outside a soon-to-be deceased person's door with a cry that sounds similar to dewch (Welsh for 'come'). The bird has no feathers or wings.

claims.statement: Referenced twice in the Welsh-language Bible.
claims.statement_id: Disebut dua kali dalam Alkitab berbahasa Welsh.
claims.quote: The Aderyn y Corff is referenced twice in the Welsh-language version of the bible, which some authors have claimed is the origin of the superstition.

claims.statement: Possibly a screech owl drawn by a patient's room light.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin burung hantu yang tertarik cahaya kamar orang sakit.
claims.quote: Many contemporary accounts of the corpse bird have suggested that it is actually a screech owl, drawn to lights coming from the room of a patient.

claims.statement: es article: British Goblins (1881) by Wirt Sikes.
claims.statement_id: Artikel es: British Goblins (1881) karya Wirt Sikes.
claims.quote: Una de las fuentes más importantes que la menciona es British Goblins (1881), obra de Wirt Sikes, recopilador de mitología y supersticiones galesas.

claims.statement: In the ancient tradition recorded by Sikes, the bird had no feathers or wings, soared without support high in the heavens, and, when not engaged on an earthly message, dwelt in the land of illusion and phantasy.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi kuno yang dicatat Sikes, burung ini tidak berbulu dan tidak bersayap, melayang tanpa tumpuan tinggi di langit, dan ketika tidak mengemban pesan duniawi ia tinggal di negeri ilusi dan khayal.
claims.quote: In ancient tradition, it had no feathers nor wings, soaring without support high in the heavens, and, when not engaged upon some earthly message, dwelling in the land of illusion and phantasy.

claims.statement: Sikes says this corpse-bird may properly be associated with the superstition about the screech-owl, whose cry near a sick-bed is held to portend death.
claims.statement_id: Sikes menyatakan burung mayat ini dapat dikaitkan dengan takhayul tentang burung hantu pekik, yang tangisannya di dekat ranjang orang sakit dipercaya pasti menandakan kematian.
claims.quote: This corpse-bird may properly be associated with the superstition regarding the screech-owl, whose cry near a sick-bed inevitably portends death.

claims.statement: Sikes notes that death portents exist in every country in endless variety, and that in Wales they take distinct and striking individualities.
claims.statement_id: Sikes mencatat bahwa pertanda kematian ada di setiap negeri dengan ragam tak terbatas, dan di Wales pertanda itu berwujud sosok-sosok yang khas dan mencolok.
claims.quote: There are death portents in every country, and in endless variety; in Wales these portents assume distinct and striking individualities

claims.statement: According to Owen, this was a bird that came flapping its wings against the window of a sick person's room, and its visit was considered a certain omen of that person's death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Owen, burung ini datang mengepakkan sayap ke jendela kamar orang sakit, dan kedatangannya dianggap pertanda pasti kematian orang itu.
claims.quote: This was a bird that came flapping its wings against the window of the room in which lay a sick person, and this visit was considered a certain omen of that person's death.

claims.statement: Owen writes that the bird singled out for the dismal honour of being a death prognosticator was the tawny, or screech owl.
claims.statement_id: Owen menulis bahwa burung yang dipilih untuk tugas muram sebagai peramal kematian itu adalah burung hantu cokelat atau burung hantu pekik.
claims.quote: The bird, singled out for the dismal honour of being a death prognosticator, was the tawny, or screech owl.

claims.statement: Basty/Bastı (Bastırık), nightmare jinn of Turkish, Altai, Tatar myth; nightmares, weakness, breathlessness; Anatolian: bastırık = nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Basty/Bastı (Bastırık), jin mimpi buruk mitologi Turki (Türk), Altai (Altay), Tatar; mimpi buruk, lemas, sesak napas; Anatolia: bastırık = mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: Bastı - Türk, Altay ve Tatar mitolojilerinde kabus cini. Bastırık (Bastırığ, Bastırı) da denilir. İnsanların kâbus görmesi, halsizleşmesi, korkuyla uyanması, sonrasında nefesinin kesilmesi bu kötücül ruh ile bağlantılı görülür.

claims.statement: Can change shape, loves cat disguise.
claims.statement_id: Dapat berubah wujud, suka menyamar sebagai kucing.
claims.quote: Değişik şekillere girebilir. Kedi kılığına bürünmeyi çok sever.

claims.statement: Albastı: a tall, white-skinned, naked devilish female.
claims.statement_id: Albastı: perempuan jahat tinggi, berkulit putih, telanjang.
claims.quote: Albastı: "Aleybanı, Alyabani." Uzun boylu, beyaz tenli ve çıplak olarak tasvir edilen şeytani dişi varlık.

claims.statement: Kulbastı: sleeps in the grave by day, rises at night; hairy, huge, smelly.
claims.statement_id: Kulbastı: tidur di kubur siang, bangkit malam; berbulu, besar, bau.
claims.quote: Kulbastı: "Kuleybanı, Gulyabani." Gündüzleri mezarda uyuyup geceleri kalktığına inanılır. Tüylü, çok büyük ve pis kokulu olarak betimlenir.

claims.statement: From the root bas- (to press); also prison and weight.
claims.statement_id: Dari akar kata bas- (menekan); juga berarti penjara dan beban.
claims.quote: (Bas) kökünden türemiştir. Basmak anlamını içerir. Hapishane anlamına da gelir. Ayrıca ağırlık demektir.

claims.statement: Karabastı: nightmare jinn sitting on chests at night, stopping breath.
claims.statement_id: Karabastı: jin mimpi buruk yang menindih dada orang malam hari hingga napas terhenti.
claims.quote: Karabastı: Kâbus, kötü rüya. Kâbus cini olarak da bilinir. Geceleri insanların göğüslerine çökerek soluklarını keser.

claims.statement: According to this journal article's abstract, the albastı is known to haunt women postpartum and newborn babies and is a female spirit designed with an evil spirit.
claims.statement_id: Menurut abstrak artikel jurnal ini, albastı dikenal menghantui perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan bayi baru lahir, dan digambarkan sebagai roh perempuan yang berkaitan dengan roh jahat.
claims.quote: Known to haunt women postpartum and newborn babies, "albastı" is a female spirit designed with an evil spirit.

claims.statement: The same abstract says the dangerous creature is found in barns, haystacks, ruins, desolate places and water sources, and is feared to rip out the liver of the puerperal woman and her baby.
claims.statement_id: Abstrak yang sama menyebut makhluk berbahaya ini ditemukan di kandang, tumpukan jerami, reruntuhan, tempat sepi, dan sumber air, serta ditakuti karena dapat merobek hati perempuan nifas dan bayinya.
claims.quote: The person who catches the dangerous creature found in barns, haystacks, ruins, desolate places, and water sources, which is feared to rip out the liver of the puerperal and her baby

claims.statement: Billy Blind (Billy Blin, Billy Blynde, Billie Blin, Belly Blin), an English and Lowland Scottish household spirit like a brownie; only in ballads, an adviser.
claims.statement_id: Billy Blind (Billy Blin, Billy Blynde, Billie Blin, Belly Blin), roh rumah Inggris (English) dan Dataran Rendah Skotlandia (Lowland Scottish), mirip brownie; hanya dalam balada, penasihat.
claims.quote: is an English and Lowland Scottish household spirit, much like a brownie. He appears only in ballads, where he frequently advises the characters.

claims.statement: Possibly a folk memory of Woden or Odin; same as Blind Harie in Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin kenangan rakyat tentang Woden atau Odin; sama dengan Blind Harie di Skotlandia (Scotland).
claims.quote: It is possible that the character of Billy Blind is a folk memory of the god Woden or Odin from Germanic mythology, in his "more playful aspect" and is speculated to have been the same character as Blind Harie

claims.statement: Child Ballads: Gil Brenton; the bride is not the woman beside him.
claims.statement_id: Child Ballads: Gil Brenton; pengantin bukan perempuan di sampingnya.
claims.quote: "Gil Brenton" (no. 5c)- Billy Blind advises the hero that the latter's bride is not the woman lying beside him (who is a virgin) .

claims.statement: Willie's Lady: a wax baby to undo Willie's mother's spells.
claims.statement_id: Willie's Lady: boneka lilin bayi untuk mematahkan sihir ibu Willie.
claims.quote: Billy Blind advises Willie to make a wax figure of a baby and invite his mother to the christening.

claims.statement: Young Bekie: helps Burd Isobel.
claims.statement_id: Young Bekie: membantu Burd Isobel.
claims.quote: He advises Burd Isobel that Young Bekie is about to marry another bride, and gives her assistance in the magical journey to reach him in time.

claims.statement: Peter S. Beagle's Tamsin (1999); Renegade Nell (2023), Nick Mohammed.
claims.statement_id: Tamsin (1999) karya Peter S. Beagle; Renegade Nell (2023), Nick Mohammed.
claims.quote: In modern fantasy, Billy Blind appears in Peter S. Beagle's Tamsin (1999), in which his main characteristic is to give advice.

claims.statement: pt article: appears only in ballads, often advising characters.
claims.statement_id: Artikel pt: hanya muncul dalam balada, sering menasihati tokoh.
claims.quote: Aparece, entretanto, somente em baladas, onde muitas vezes aconselha as personagens.

claims.statement: Blunderbore (Blunderboar, Thunderbore, Blunderbus, Blunderbuss), a giant of Cornish and English folklore; Jack the Giant Killer; Penwith; brother Rebecks.
claims.statement_id: Blunderbore (Blunderboar, Thunderbore, Blunderbus, Blunderbuss), raksasa folklor Cornwall (Cornish) dan Inggris (English); Jack the Giant Killer; Penwith; saudara Rebecks.
claims.quote: is a giant of Cornish and English folklore. A number of folk and fairy tales include a giant named Blunderbore, most notably "Jack the Giant Killer". The stories usually associate him with the area of Penwith.

claims.statement: Lived at Ludgvan Lese, terrorising travellers to St Ives; the Jack and the Beanstalk ogre.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di Ludgvan Lese, meneror pelancong ke St Ives; ogre Jack and the Beanstalk.
claims.quote: Cornish folklore remembers Blunderbore as living in Ludgvan Lese (a manor in Ludgvan), where he terrorized travelers heading north to St Ives.

claims.statement: Joseph Jacobs's version: kidnaps three lords and ladies.
claims.statement_id: Versi Joseph Jacobs: menculik tiga bangsawan dan istrinya.
claims.quote: In the version recorded by Joseph Jacobs, Blunderbore lives in Penwith, where he kidnaps three lords and ladies, planning to eat the men and make the women his wives.

claims.statement: Jack nooses Blunderbore and Rebecks and slits their throats; Jack killed Cormoran.
claims.statement_id: Jack menjerat Blunderbore dan Rebecks lalu menggorok leher mereka; Jack membunuh Cormoran.
claims.quote: When the giants arrive, he drops the nooses, slides down the rope, and slits their throats.

claims.statement: Tom the Tinkeard: hedge over the highway St Ives–Marazion; twenty women abducted.
claims.statement_id: Tom the Tinkeard: pagar di jalan raya St Ives–Marazion; dua puluh perempuan diculik.
claims.quote: Here, Blunderbore has built a hedge over the King's Highway between St Ives to Marazion, claiming the land as his own.

claims.statement: ca article: a giant of Cornish and English mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ca: raksasa mitologi Cornwall dan Inggris.
claims.quote: Blunderbore (també anomenat Blunderboar, Thunderbore, Blunderbus, o Blunderbuss) és un gegant de la mitologia còrnica i anglesa.

claims.statement: Bodach (bodaich; Old Irish botach), trickster or bogeyman of Gaelic folklore; paired with the cailleach in Irish legend.
claims.statement_id: Bodach (bodaich; botach Irlandia Kuno, Old Irish), penipu atau momok folklor Gaelik (Gaelic); pasangan cailleach dalam legenda Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: is a trickster or bogeyman figure in Gaelic folklore and mythology. The bodach "old man" is paired with the cailleach "hag, old woman" in Irish legend.

claims.statement: Irish word for tenant, serf; from bod (tail, penis) + -ach; modern Gaelic: old man.
claims.statement_id: Kata Irlandia untuk penyewa, budak tani; dari bod (ekor, penis) + -ach; Gaelik modern: lelaki tua.
claims.quote: Bodach (Old Irish also botach ) is the Irish word for a tenant, a serf or peasant. It is derived from bod (Old Irish bod ) "tail, penis".

claims.statement: Eachtra Bhodaigh an Chóta Lachtna (16th/17th c.): identified with Manannán mac Lir; bugbear, devil.
claims.statement_id: Eachtra Bhodaigh an Chóta Lachtna (abad ke-16/17): disamakan dengan Manannán mac Lir; momok, iblis.
claims.quote: In the early modern (16th or 17th century) tale Eachtra Bhodaigh an Chóta Lachtna , the bodach is identified with the Manannán mac Lir .

claims.statement: Scottish folklore: comes down the chimney to kidnap naughty children.
claims.statement_id: Folklor Skotlandia (Scottish): turun lewat cerobong menculik anak nakal.
claims.quote: In Scottish folklore the bodach comes down the chimney to kidnap naughty children, used as a cautionary tale or bogeyman figure to frighten children into good behaviour.

claims.statement: Bodach Glas (Old Grey Man), death omen; Walter Scott's Waverley, Fergus Mac-Ivor.
claims.statement_id: Bodach Glas (Lelaki Tua Kelabu) pertanda maut; Waverley karya Walter Scott, Fergus Mac-Ivor.
claims.quote: A related being known as the Bodach Glas ("Old Grey Man") is considered an omen of death. In Walter Scott's novel, Waverley, Fergus Mac-Ivor sees a Bodach Glas , which foretells his death.

claims.statement: it article: Bodach (old man), a Scottish spirit like the Bogeyman.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: Bodach (lelaki tua), roh mitologi Skotlandia mirip Bogeyman.
claims.quote: Il Bodach (scozzese: "Vecchio Uomo") è uno spirito della mitologia scozzese simile al Bogeyman.

claims.statement: Bran and Sceólang (raven and survivor), hounds of Fionn mac Cumhaill, Fenian Cycle of Irish myth; white, purple haunches, crimson tail, blue feet.
claims.statement_id: Bran dan Sceólang (gagak dan penyintas), anjing Fionn mac Cumhaill, Siklus Fenian (Fenian Cycle) mitologi Irlandia (Irish); putih, pinggul ungu, ekor merah, kaki biru.
claims.quote: are the hounds of Fionn mac Cumhaill in the Fenian Cycle of Irish mythology. The dogs are described as being mostly white, with purple haunches, a crimson tail, blue feet, and standing as tall as Fionn's shoulder.

claims.statement: Bran red ears, green back, yellow feet; Bran male, Sceólang female.
claims.statement_id: Bran bertelinga merah, punggung hijau, kaki kuning; Bran jantan, Sceólang betina.
claims.quote: Other sources describe Bran as having red ears, a green back, white underbelly, black sides, and yellow feet. Bran is usually male, while Sceólang is usually female

claims.statement: Their mother Uirne was turned into a dog while pregnant.
claims.statement_id: Ibu mereka Uirne diubah menjadi anjing saat hamil.
claims.quote: The hounds' mother, Uirne, was transformed into a dog while pregnant, hence the canine birth of her twin children.

claims.statement: Uirne sister of Muirne, Fionn's mother; the hounds are Fionn's cousins.
claims.statement_id: Uirne saudari Muirne, ibu Fionn; anjing-anjing itu sepupu Fionn.
claims.quote: As Uirne is the sister of Fionn's mother Muirne, Bran and Sceólang would be their masters' cousins.

claims.statement: ga article: Bran agus Sceólang, Fionn's hounds in the Fiannaíocht.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ga: Bran agus Sceólang, anjing Fionn dalam Fiannaíocht.
claims.quote: San Fhiannaíocht i miotaseolaíocht na nGael, cúnna Fhionn mhic Cumhaill ba ea Bran agus Sceólang (Fiach Dubh agus Scéalaí).

claims.statement: They found Oisín, Fionn's son, naked in the forest; Sceólang died hunting; Bran drowned.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menemukan Oisín, putra Fionn, telanjang di hutan; Sceólang mati berburu; Bran tenggelam.
claims.quote: Dar le seanscéal, ba iadsan a tháinig ar Oisín mac Fhionn ar fáin lomnocht san fhoraois.

claims.statement: Y Fuwch Frech (speckled cow), a cow of Welsh folklore; Elias Owen: Freckled Cow.
claims.statement_id: Y Fuwch Frech (Buwch Frech, sapi berbintik), sapi folklor Welsh (Wales); Elias Owen: Freckled Cow.
claims.quote: Y Fuwch Frech (Welsh: literally the speckled/brindled cow) is a cow in Welsh folklore. She was described by Elias Owen as the "Freckled Cow".

claims.statement: 1887 eisteddfod essay; Denbighshire: milk for the needy; a witch milked her dry; plunged into a lake near Cerrig-y-drudion with two oxen (Ychen Bannog).
claims.statement_id: Esai eisteddfod 1887; Denbighshire: susu untuk yang membutuhkan; penyihir memerah kering; terjun ke danau dekat Cerrig-y-drudion dengan dua anak sapi jantan (Ychen Bannog).
claims.quote: he recorded a story from Denbighshire of a cow which was said to give milk to "any one ... in want of milk" until a witch milked the cow dry. The cow then left, plunging into a lake near Cerrig-y-drudion, and leading her two children, long-horned oxen

claims.statement: Fairy cows of abundant milk from and back to lakes across Wales.
claims.statement_id: Sapi peri bersusu melimpah dari dan ke danau di seluruh Wales.
claims.quote: The idea of fairy cows with abundant milk which came from and returned to lakes occurs across Wales

claims.statement: A similar cow in Shropshire: The White Cow of Mitchell's Fold.
claims.statement_id: Sapi serupa di Shropshire: The White Cow of Mitchell's Fold.
claims.quote: Owen likewise linked his Freckled Cow with a number of similar cows such as one over the border in Shropshire: "There she is known as The White Cow of Mitchell's Fold".

claims.statement: cy article: Buwch Fraith Hiraethog, Mynydd Hiraethog; white with pink speckles; endless milk; Ychen Bannog.
claims.statement_id: Artikel cy: Buwch Fraith Hiraethog, Mynydd Hiraethog; putih dengan bintik merah muda; susu tak habis; Ychen Bannog.
claims.quote: Yn ei draethawd ar lên gwerin, ar gyfer Eisteddfod Genedlaethol 1887, disgrifia Elias Owen stori am fuwch hudol o ardal Mynydd Hiraethog. Roedd yn wyn pur gyda brychni pinc ac roedd ganddi gyflwenwad diddiwedd o lefrith.

claims.statement: In the tale Owen records, whoever was in want of milk came with a vessel, and however big it was they always left with the pail filled with rich milk.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah yang dicatat Owen, siapa pun yang butuh susu datang membawa wadah, dan sebesar apa pun wadah itu mereka selalu pulang dengan ember penuh susu kental.
claims.quote: Whenever any one was in want of milk they went to this cow, taking with them a vessel into which they milked the cow, and, however big this vessel was, they always departed with the pail filled with rich milk

claims.statement: In Owen's version, a wicked hag, filled with envy at the people's prosperity, determined to milk the cow dry.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Owen, seorang perempuan tua jahat yang iri pada kemakmuran orang-orang bertekad memerah sapi itu sampai kering.
claims.quote: At last a wicked hag, filled with envy at the people's prosperity, determined to milk the cow dry

claims.statement: After this treatment the cow immediately left the country and was never seen again.
claims.statement_id: Setelah diperlakukan demikian, sapi itu segera meninggalkan negeri itu dan tidak pernah terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: the cow immediately, upon this treatment, left the country, and was never more seen.

claims.statement: Owen notes that the site of the cow house is still pointed out and keeps the name Preseb y Fuwch Frech.
claims.statement_id: Owen mencatat bahwa lokasi kandang sapi itu masih ditunjukkan dan tetap bernama Preseb y Fuwch Frech.
claims.quote: The site of the cow house is still pointed out, and retains its name, Preseb y Fuwch Frech

claims.statement: In a book Owen cites, vulgar opinion held that a large bone at Gwydir was the rib of the Dun Cow (y Fuwch Frech), killed by the Earl of Warwick.
claims.statement_id: Dalam buku yang dikutip Owen, menurut pendapat awam sebuah tulang besar di Gwydir adalah tulang rusuk Dun Cow (y Fuwch Frech) yang dibunuh Earl of Warwick.
claims.quote: it is the rib of the Dun Cow (y Fuwch Frech), killed by the Earl of Warwick.

claims.statement: Ghost of stable boy Robert Skelton, Hylton Castle, Sunderland, Northern England; 16th or 17th century.
claims.statement_id: Hantu Robert Skelton, pemuda kandang, di Kastel (Castle) Hylton, Sunderland, Inggris Utara (Northern England); abad ke-16 atau ke-17.
claims.quote: The Cauld Lad of Hylton is a ghost of murdered stable boy Robert Skelton, said to haunt the ruins of Hylton Castle (in Sunderland, Northern England). The events are said to have taken place in the 16th or 17th century

claims.statement: Courted Baron Hylton's daughter; or overslept and was killed; body in a pond or well.
claims.statement_id: Mendekati putri Baron Hylton; atau kesiangan dan dibunuh; jasad di kolam atau sumur.
claims.quote: One story states that the stable boy was caught courting Baron Hylton's daughter, and was killed. Another version says that the baron ordered that his horse be prepared for an important journey, but Skelton had overslept.

claims.statement: The kitchen tidied or messed at night.
claims.statement_id: Dapur dirapikan atau diacak di malam hari.
claims.quote: The kitchen would be tidied at night if left in a mess, or messed up if left tidy.

claims.statement: The cook saw a naked boy's ghost crying I'm cauld; given a warm cloak, he left.
claims.statement_id: Juru masak melihat hantu anak telanjang menangis I'm cauld; diberi jubah hangat, ia pergi.
claims.quote: He saw the ghost of a naked boy, and heard him crying "I'm cauld" ("I'm cold"). The cook and his wife left a warm cloak for the ghost

claims.statement: Like a poltergeist; other versions: elf, barghest or enchanted brownie.
claims.statement_id: Mirip poltergeist; versi lain: elf, barghest atau brownie terkutuk.
claims.quote: Other versions of the tale describe the Cauld Lad as an elf, barghest, or brownie who is under a spell from which he can only be released by being given a gift.

claims.statement: fr article: the ghost of stable boy Robert Skelton.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: hantu pemuda kandang Robert Skelton.
claims.quote: sont réputées hantées par le fantôme du jeune garçon d'étable Robert Skelton, connu également sous le nom de Cauld Lad of Hylton.

claims.statement: Cofgod (Cofgodas), Old English term for a household god of Anglo-Saxon paganism; England.
claims.statement_id: Cofgod (Cofgodas), istilah bahasa Inggris Kuno (Old English) untuk dewa rumah tangga paganisme Anglo-Saxon; Inggris.
claims.quote: was an Old English term for a household god in Anglo-Saxon paganism.

claims.statement: Ken Dowden: equivalent of the Penates of Ancient Rome; compared to the Kobold; from the kofewalt, spirit of a room.
claims.statement_id: Ken Dowden: setara Penates Roma Kuno (Ancient Rome); dibandingkan dengan Kobold; dari kofewalt, roh penguasa ruangan.
claims.quote: The classicist Ken Dowden opined that the cofgodas were the equivalent of the Penates found in Ancient Rome. Dowden also compared them to the Kobold of later continental folklore, arguing that they had both originated from the kofewalt, a spirit that had power over a room.

claims.statement: The English hob and Anglo-Celtic brownie may be modern survivals of the cofgod.
claims.statement_id: Hob Inggris (English) dan brownie Anglo-Kelt (Anglo-Celtic) mungkin sisa modern cofgod.
claims.quote: If it is true that such beings were known to the early English, later legendary beings such as the English hob and Anglo-Celtic brownie would be the modern survival of the cofgod.

claims.statement: Only instance: a gloss on Latin penates.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya kemunculan: glos untuk kata Latin penates.
claims.quote: However, the only instance of the word cofgodas in Old English is as a gloss (an explanatory definition) to the Latin word penates.

claims.statement: ko article: Old English term for a household god in Anglo-Saxon paganism.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ko: istilah Inggris Kuno untuk dewa rumah dalam paganisme Anglo-Saxon.
claims.quote: 코프갓(Cofgod)은 앵글로색슨 이교에서 가택신을 가리키던 고대 영어 용어이다.

claims.statement: The plural Cofgodas, glossed 'cove-gods', was an Old English term for a household god.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk jamaknya Cofgodas, yang diberi arti "dewa-ruang" (cove-gods), adalah istilah bahasa Inggris Kuno untuk dewa rumah tangga.
claims.quote: (plural Cofgodas ("cove-gods")) was an Old English term for a household god

claims.statement: Dragon of Mordiford, near Mordiford, Herefordshire, England; confluence of the River Lugg and River Wye.
claims.statement_id: Naga Mordiford (Dragon of Mordiford), dekat desa Mordiford, Herefordshire, Inggris; pertemuan Sungai (River) Lugg dan Wye.
claims.quote: The Dragon of Mordiford is a legendary creature that was said to reside just outside the Herefordshire village of Mordiford, at the confluence of the River Lugg and the River Wye.

claims.statement: A wyvern found by the girl Maud in the forest; fed milk; winged.
claims.statement_id: Wyvern ditemukan gadis Maud di hutan; diberi susu; bersayap.

claims.statement: The emerald dragon killed livestock and farmers; spared Maud.
claims.statement_id: Naga hijau zamrud memangsa ternak dan petani; tak menyakiti Maud.
claims.quote: Soon, it began to plague the local farms, killing their livestock, especially cows and sheep, and farmers were intolerant.

claims.statement: Garstone deflected the fire blast, lanced the throat; Maud mourned.
claims.statement_id: Garstone menangkis semburan api, menusuk leher dengan tombak; Maud meratap.
claims.quote: The dragon almost instantly released a blast of fire, Garstone barely deflecting it. He aimed a lance at the wyvern's throat, releasing it and fully penetrating through the dragon.

claims.statement: A convict in a cider barrel at the River Lugg shot the dragon's heart.
claims.statement_id: Narapidana dalam tong sari apel di Sungai (River) Lugg memanah jantung naga.
claims.quote: He then concealed himself in the barrel at the River Lugg, where the serpent drank its water. Once the dragon arrived at the river, the convict shot an arrow through a hole in the barrel, piercing the creature's heart.

claims.statement: The dragon's poison flowed into the barrel, killing the convict.

claims.quote: モーディフォードの竜（モーディフォードのりゅう、英: Dragon of Mordiford。モーディフォード・ドラゴンとも）は、英国ヘレフォードシャーモーディフォード村（Mordiford）の伝承である。

claims.statement: Drummer of Cortachy, a spirit of Cortachy Castle, Scotland; omen of death for the Ogilvy family, Earl of Airlie; nine feet; ghostly pipes.
claims.statement_id: Penabuh Drum Cortachy (Drummer of Cortachy), roh di Kastel (Castle) Cortachy, Skotlandia; pertanda kematian keluarga Ogilvy, Earl of Airlie; sembilan kaki; pipa hantu.
claims.quote: The Drummer of Cortachy is the name given to a spirit who is thought to haunt Cortachy Castle. There are many interpretations of the story, but he is variously thought to portend the death of a member of the Ogilvy family, Earl of Airlie or the owners of Cortachy Castle. He is said to be nine foot tall

claims.statement: Roots in the 19th century, death of the 14th Earl of Airlie; plays a tattoo.
claims.statement_id: Akar abad ke-19, kematian Earl of Airlie ke-14 (14th); memainkan tattoo.
claims.quote: The legend can trace its roots back to at least the 19th century and the death of the 14th Earl of Airlie. He is said to play a tattoo when he appears.

claims.statement: Spirit of a Carlisle family drummer thrown from the tower by a jealous Lord; stuffed into his drum.
claims.statement_id: Roh penabuh drum keluarga Carlisle dilempar dari menara karena cemburu Lord; dijejalkan ke dalam drum.
claims.quote: The ghost is thought to be the spirit of a drummer for the Carlisle family; who was thrown out of a window in the high tower of the castle after incurring the jealousy of the then Lord.

claims.statement: 1844 sighting, Lady Airlie heard drumming; died June 1845.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan 1844, Lady Airlie mendengar drum; meninggal Juni 1845.
claims.quote: The most famous sighting of the drummer is said to have occurred in 1844, when Lady Airlie (or, in some versions of the tale, her guests) reportedly heard the mysterious drumming noise.

claims.statement: The spirit dormant; the Earl of Airlie died in the Boer War, 1900.
claims.statement_id: Roh kini tidur; Earl of Airlie gugur di Perang Boer (Boer War) 1900.
claims.quote: The spirit is now thought to be dormant since in 1900 the Earl of Airlie died in the Boer War without a reported sighting.

claims.statement: as article: spirit dormant since the Earl of Airlie's death in the Boer War, 1900.
claims.statement_id: Artikel as: roh dianggap tidur sejak kematian Earl of Airlie dalam Perang Boer 1900.

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk mitologi atau cerita rakyat: artikel membahas klaim kasus poltergeist tahun 1661 di rumah John Mompesson di Tedworth (Tidworth, Wiltshire) yang dicatat Joseph Glanvill dalam Saducismus Triumphatus (1681), yaitu peristiwa sejarah yang diklaim terjadi dan melibatkan orang nyata (penabuh drum William Drury), bukan sosok dalam tradisi.
