claims.statement: Ellén Trechend, a three-headed monster of Irish myth; Cath Maige Mucrama; cave of Cruachan (Rathcroghan, County Roscommon); killed by Amergin, Ulaid poet.
claims.statement_id: Ellén Trechend, monster berkepala tiga mitologi Irlandia (Irish, Ireland); Cath Maige Mucrama (Pertempuran Mag Mucrima); gua Cruachan (Rathcroghan, County Roscommon); dibunuh Amergin, penyair Ulaid.
claims.quote: The Ellén Trechend is a three-headed monster referred to in Irish mythology. It is mentioned in the text Cath Maige Mucrama (The Battle of Mag Mucrima) as having emerged from the cave of Cruachan (Rathcroghan, County Roscommon) and laid waste to Ireland until it was killed by the Ulaid poet and hero Amergin.

claims.statement: Interpretations: swarm of three-headed creatures; Whitley Stokes: monstrous bird; T. F. O'Rahilly: Aillén, foe of Fionn mac Cumhaill.
claims.statement_id: Tafsiran: kawanan makhluk berkepala tiga; Whitley Stokes: burung raksasa; T. F. O'Rahilly: Aillén, lawan Fionn mac Cumhaill.
claims.quote: One translator interprets it as a "swarm of three-headed creatures"; Whitley Stokes offered a "monstrous triple-headed bird" (Old Irish én, "bird"); while T. F. O'Rahilly identifies it with Aillén, the fire-breathing monster fought by Fionn mac Cumhaill.

claims.statement: P. W. Joyce: the Sidhe of Cruachan opened at Samhain; goblins and copper-red birds led by a three-headed vulture.
claims.statement_id: P. W. Joyce: Sidhe Cruachan terbuka saat Samhain; goblin dan burung merah tembaga dipimpin nasar berkepala tiga.
claims.quote: he tells how the Sidhe of Cruachan opened on Samhain and a crowd of horrible goblins rushed out, along with a flock of copper-red birds who were led by a monstrous three-headed vulture.

claims.statement: ga article: Eilléan Trícheann, a monster of Gaelic myth; Ráth Cruachan; Amergin.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ga: Eilléan Trícheann, monster mitologi Gaelik; Ráth Cruachan; Amergin.
claims.quote: Is arracht i miotaseolaíocht na nGael é Eilléan Trícheann (Sean-Ghaeilge: Ellén Trechend).

claims.statement: In the translation of Cath Maige Mucrama, the swarm of three-headed creatures came out of that cave and laid Ireland waste until Amairgene, father of Conall Cernach, destroyed it in the presence of all the Ulaid.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Cath Maige Mucrama, kawanan makhluk berkepala tiga keluar dari gua itu dan menghancurkan Irlandia sampai Amairgene, ayah Conall Cernach, membinasakannya di hadapan seluruh Ulaid.
claims.quote: Out of it too came the swarm of three-headed creatures that laid Ireland waste until Amairgene father of Conall Cernach, fighting alone (?), destroyed it in the presence of all the Ulaid.

claims.statement: The same text says Mag Mucrima was named for magic pigs that had come out of a cave.
claims.statement_id: Teks yang sama menyebut Mag Mucrima dinamai dari babi-babi ajaib yang keluar dari sebuah gua.
claims.quote: Now Mag Mucrima [was so called from] magic pigs that had come out of the cave of

claims.statement: Its name is difficult to interpret: trechend means 'three-headed', but ellén is an obscure word.
claims.statement_id: Namanya sulit ditafsirkan: trechend berarti "berkepala tiga", sedangkan ellén adalah kata yang kabur.
claims.quote: Its name is difficult to interpret: trechend means "three-headed", but ellén is an obscure word.

claims.statement: Fions, lutin-like little people of Upper Brittany's maritime folklore; maybe English in origin; Paul Sébillot, late 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Fions, mirip lutin, bangsa kecil folklor maritim Haute-Bretagne (Upper Brittany, Prancis); mungkin asal Inggris (English); Paul Sébillot akhir abad ke-19.
claims.quote: Fions are lutin-like creatures of the little people, mostly mentioned in the maritime folklore of Upper Brittany. They might be of English origin. Most of the stories about them come from Paul Sébillot's collections in the late 19th century.

claims.statement: Live in rocks and caves of Brittany's north shore; servants of the houles fairies; battalions; war on a golden ship.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di batu dan gua pantai utara Bretagne (Brittany); pelayan peri houle; batalion; perang melawan kapal emas.
claims.quote: Characterized by their habitat in the rocks and caves of Brittany's northern shores, the Fions lead a military life in community with the houles fairies, as their servants. Organized into battalions, they are said to wage war on a golden ship.

claims.statement: Graze livestock, give enchanted objects or food.
claims.statement_id: Menggembalakan ternak, memberi benda ajaib atau makanan.
claims.quote: According to tales, they own and graze livestock, and sometimes give enchanted objects or food to humans.

claims.statement: Paul Sébillot: no female Fions; Pierre Dubois: hermaphrodite; Françoise Morvan: kin of Anglo-Saxon fairies, Jetins.
claims.statement_id: Paul Sébillot: tak ada Fions betina; Pierre Dubois: hermafrodit; Françoise Morvan: kerabat peri Anglo-Saxon, Jetins.
claims.quote: Opinions differ on this point, for while Paul Sébillot says "there were no female Fions, at least in the houles", Pierre Dubois believes they are hermaphroditic creatures.

claims.statement: fr article: little people of Haute-Bretagne maritime folklore, lutin-like, maybe English.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: bangsa kecil folklor maritim Haute-Bretagne, mirip lutin, mungkin asal Inggris.
claims.quote: Les Fions sont des créatures du petit peuple surtout mentionnées dans le folklore maritime de la Haute-Bretagne, de type lutin et peut-être d'origine anglaise.

claims.statement: In Sébillot's tale "La fée de la Corbière", as the thread was spun, a regiment of little fions took it, wound it and wove it, and it took them little time to make a piece of cloth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah "La fée de la Corbière" karya Sébillot, seiring benang dipintal, sepasukan fions kecil mengambil benang itu, menggulung dan menenunnya, dan hanya sebentar mereka membuat selembar kain.
claims.quote: À mesure que le fil se faisait et se déroulait, un régiment de petits fions prenaient le fil, le dévidaient, le tissaient et ils n’étaient guère de temps à faire une pièce de toile.

claims.statement: In the same tale, when the meal was over, one of the little fions began to sing and the others repeated it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang sama, setelah santap selesai, seorang fion kecil mulai bernyanyi dan yang lain mengulanginya.
claims.quote: Quand le repas fut fini, un des petits fions se mit à chanter ; les autres répétaient

claims.statement: Firedrakes (fire-drake, fyrdraca) of English folklore: dragon-sightings from shooting stars and will-o'-the-wisps; fireballs in the sky; Shakespeare.
claims.statement_id: Firedrake (fire-drake, fyrdraca) folklor Inggris (English): penampakan naga dari bintang jatuh dan will-o'-the-wisp; bola api di langit; Shakespeare.
claims.quote: Firedrakes are dragon-sightings stemming from shooting stars and will-o'-the-wisps, said to appear as dragon-shaped fireballs or sparking streaks of fire in the sky, and the term also appears as a synonym for the above, including "fiery dragon" and "fiery meteor".

claims.statement: Thought to be the Devil in dragon shape.
claims.statement_id: Dianggap Iblis (Devil) dalam wujud naga.
claims.quote: While not unique to English folklore, the firedrake have often been thought to be the Devil himself in dragon shape.

claims.statement: Native drake (Old English draca), not French dragon; Beowulf, 8th–9th century.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk drake (Inggris Kuno, Old English: draca), bukan dragon Prancis (French); Beowulf abad ke-8 hingga ke-9.
claims.quote: The term firedrake utilizes the inherited indigenous form drake (Old English: draca ), instead of the more common French borrowing dragon (Old French: dragon ). The construction appears as early as Beowulf from the 8th to the 9th century

claims.statement: Shakespeare, Henry VIII: a red-nosed brazier called a firedrake.
claims.statement_id: Shakespeare, Henry VIII: tukang patri berhidung merah disebut firedrake.
claims.quote: Shakespeare in Henry VIII comically describes a tinker or brazier (who works with fire) as a red-nosed "firedrake"

claims.statement: ja article: Beowulf's fire dragon (fyr draca) is a fire drake, a Germanic fire dragon.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ja: naga api Beowulf (fyr draca) adalah fire drake, naga api Jermanik.
claims.quote: 英雄詩『ベーオウルフ』の主人公が対峙する「火竜」（古英語: fyr draca）も、現代語でいえばファイアー・ドレイクであり、広義的にはゲルマン（チュートン人）全般のの火竜のことである

claims.statement: Murray's dictionary defines the fire-drake as a mythical creature belonging to Germanic superstition.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Murray mendefinisikan fire-drake sebagai makhluk mitos yang termasuk dalam takhayul Jermanik.
claims.quote: a mythical creature belonging to Germanic superstition.

claims.statement: The same dictionary lists a sense of fire-drake as a fiery meteor, citing W. Fulke, Meteors, on flying dragons that Englishmen call fire-drakes.
claims.statement_id: Kamus yang sama mencantumkan arti fire-drake sebagai meteor berapi, dengan kutipan W. Fulke, Meteors, tentang naga terbang yang oleh orang Inggris disebut fire-drake.
claims.quote: A fiery meteor. ... Flying Dragons, or as Englishmen call them, fire-Drakes, be caused in this manor.

claims.statement: The dictionary cites Gower, Conf., which says that sometimes it seems the fire-drake, and so the lewd people judge it.
claims.statement_id: Kamus itu mengutip Gower, Conf., yang menulis bahwa kadang-kadang tampak sebagai fire-drake dan demikianlah orang awam menilainya.
claims.quote: Somtime the fire-drake it semeth, And so the lewde people it demeth.

claims.statement: Gaillimh inion Breasail, the mythical woman behind the name of the river and city of Galway, Ireland; James Hardiman quoting Lughaidh Ó Cléirigh; drowned in the river.
claims.statement_id: Gaillimh inion Breasail, perempuan mitos asal nama sungai dan kota Galway, Irlandia (Ireland); James Hardiman mengutip Lughaidh Ó Cléirigh; tenggelam di sungai.
claims.quote: Gaillimh inion Breasail is the name of the mythical woman from whom the river and city of Galway, Ireland, derives its name. According to James Hardiman, quoting Lughaidh Ó Cléirigh, "that the city of Galway took its name from the river, in which was drowned Gaillimh, the daughter of Breasail."

claims.statement: Mid-17th-century map: a rock in the river (Corrib) where a woman named Galva drowned.
claims.statement_id: Peta pertengahan abad ke-17: batu di sungai (Corrib) tempat perempuan bernama Galva tenggelam.
claims.quote: Hardiman goes on to state that in the mid-17th map of the town, "a rock is shown in the river" (now called the Corrib), "where" it is stated, that "a woman, named Galva, was drowned, near a great rock, in the river,"

claims.statement: Daughter of Breasail, a Fir Bolg chief; local river goddess like Boann (Gaelic).
claims.statement_id: Putri Breasail, kepala suku Fir Bolg; dewi sungai setempat seperti Boann (Gaelik, Gaelic).
claims.quote: She was said to be the daughter of a chief of the Fir Bolg, Breasail. It is now generally held that she was a tribal or local goddess of the river, much like other Gaelic deities such as Boann.

claims.statement: Name means stony river; late Irish prehistory.
claims.statement_id: Nama berarti sungai berbatu; prasejarah akhir Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: The etymology of the name is thought to translate, roughly, as stony river, and probably dates back to at least the late Irish pre-historic era.

claims.statement: ga article: mythical woman who named Galway city and river; daughter of Breasail, Fir Bolg chief.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ga: perempuan mitos asal nama kota dan sungai Galway; putri Breasail, kepala Fir Bolg.
claims.quote: Bean mhiotasach ab ea Gaillimh iníon Breasail as a ainmníodh cathair agus abhainn na Gaillimhe. Dúradh gurbh iníon cheannaire na bhFear Bolg, Breasail, í.

claims.statement: Hardiman writes that the old map of Galway states that a woman named Galva was drowned near a great rock in the river, and that from this circumstance the town originally took its name.
claims.statement_id: Hardiman menulis bahwa menurut peta lama Galway, seorang perempuan bernama Galva tenggelam di dekat sebuah batu besar di sungai, dan dari peristiwa itu kota tersebut mula-mula mendapat namanya.
claims.quote: a woman, named Galva, was drowned, near a great rock, in the river, (which is delineated on the map,) and that from this circumstance the town originally took its name.

claims.statement: Hardiman himself regards the traditional report as weakly founded and the story attributing the name to the woman Gaillimh, or Galva, as fabulous in complexion.
claims.statement_id: Hardiman sendiri menilai laporan tradisional itu berdasar lemah dan kisah yang menisbahkan nama kota kepada perempuan bernama Gaillimh atau Galva itu bercorak dongeng.
claims.quote: we consider the weak foundation of traditional report, and the fabulous complexion of the story, attributing the name to the woman, Gaillimh, or Galva

claims.statement: Galloway Puma, a phantom cat of Scottish folklore, Dumfries and Galloway.
claims.statement_id: Galloway Puma, kucing hantu folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Scotland), Dumfries and Galloway.
claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, the Galloway Puma is a "phantom cat" said to dwell in Dumfries and Galloway, in south-west Scotland.

claims.statement: Late 1990s, Canadian tourists saw a cougar-like animal near Kirroughtree, Newton Stewart, Galloway Forest; locals 1999.
claims.statement_id: Akhir 1990-an, wisatawan Kanada (Canadian) melihat hewan mirip cougar dekat Kirroughtree, Newton Stewart, Hutan Galloway (Galloway Forest); warga 1999.
claims.quote: The rumours of a big cat in Galloway began in the late 1990s, when Canadian tourists claimed to have seen an animal which resembled a cougar near Kirroughtree, south-east of Newton Stewart. The tourists apparently saw the animal while returning from a nature walk in the Galloway Forest.

claims.statement: Farmers and Forestry Commission workers saw a big black cat, mainly in the Machars.
claims.statement_id: Petani dan pekerja Forestry Commission melihat kucing hitam besar, terutama di Machars.
claims.quote: After this, many people, specifically farmers and Forestry Commission workers, claimed to have seen a big black cat throughout the region, but mainly in the Machars area.

claims.statement: June 2001, a woman near Newton Stewart golf course; a black cat bigger than an alsatian; fled when the dog barked.
claims.statement_id: Juni (June) 2001, perempuan dekat lapangan golf Newton Stewart; kucing hitam lebih besar dari alsatian; lari saat anjing menggonggong.
claims.quote: In June 2001, a young lady walking her dog near Newton Stewart golf course, which lies on the edge of Galloway Forest, was left startled and shaken when what she described as a "large black cat, bigger than an alsatian", sprung out at her

claims.statement: zh article: December 2012, Alan Dalton and his wife Mandy saw a labrador-sized black cat at Newton Stewart.
claims.statement_id: Artikel zh: Desember 2012, Alan Dalton dan istrinya Mandy melihat kucing hitam sebesar labrador di Newton Stewart.
claims.quote: 2012年12月，阿伦·多尔顿（Alan Dalton ）与妻子曼蒂（Mandy ）于牛顿斯图尔特看见一只拉布拉多般大小的黑色大猫。

claims.statement: According to a 2013 Galloway Gazette report, holidaymakers staying at Kirroughtee Hotel outside Newton Stewart had a close encounter with an elusive big cat, described as one of Galloway's best kept secrets.
claims.statement_id: Menurut laporan The Galloway Gazette (2013), wisatawan yang menginap di Kirroughtee Hotel di luar Newton Stewart berjumpa dekat dengan kucing besar yang sukar ditangkap, yang disebut sebagai salah satu rahasia Galloway yang paling tersembunyi.
claims.quote: Holidaymakers staying at Kirroughtee Hotel outside Newton Stewart had a close encounter with one of Galloway’s best kept secrets last Saturday morning – an elusive big cat.

claims.statement: The same report says that in the past four years 20 big cat sightings had been reported to The Galloway Gazette.
claims.statement_id: Laporan yang sama menyebut dalam empat tahun terakhir ada 20 laporan penampakan kucing besar yang masuk ke The Galloway Gazette.
claims.quote: In the past four years 20 big cat sightings have been reported to The Galloway Gazette. ... [The Galloway Gazette, 14/08/2013]

claims.statement: Welsh giants (cewri): Bendigeidfran fab Llyr, king of Britain, Second Branch of the Mabinogi; Idris Gawr, Cader Idris; Ysbaddaden Bencawr, How Culhwch won Olwen; Arthur, Gwalchmai fab Gwyar.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa (cewri) Welsh (Wales): Bendigeidfran fab Llyr, raja Britania (Britain), Cabang Kedua Mabinogi (Second Branch); Idris Gawr, Cader Idris; Ysbaddaden Bencawr, How Culhwch won Olwen; Arthur, Gwalchmai fab Gwyar.
claims.quote: Among the most notable are Bendigeidfran fab Llyr, a mythological king of Britain during the Second Branch of the Mabinogi, Idris Gawr of Cader Idris, and Ysbaddaden Bencawr, the chief antagonist of the early Arthurian tale How Culhwch won Olwen. Both Arthur and Gwalchmai fab Gwyar feature prominently as giant-slayers in Welsh tradition.

claims.statement: Geoffrey of Monmouth: the original inhabitants of Britain.
claims.statement_id: Geoffrey dari (of) Monmouth: penghuni asli Britania (Britain).
claims.quote: Giants are also described by Geoffrey of Monmouth as the original inhabitants of Britain, who were overwhelmed by human settlers.

claims.statement: Branwen ferch Llyr: Bran the Blessed; Pair Dadeni (Cauldron of Rebirth), Llassar Llaes Gyfnewid from Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Branwen ferch Llyr: Bran the Blessed; Pair Dadeni (Kuali, Cauldron of Rebirth), Llassar Llaes Gyfnewid dari Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: In the Second Branch of the Mabinogi, Branwen ferch Llyr, Britain is ruled by the giant Bran the Blessed, who has never been able to fit inside any dwelling.

claims.statement: Culhwch and Olwen: Ysbaddaden, Olwen's father, slain by Goreu fab Custennin.
claims.statement_id: Culhwch and Olwen: Ysbaddaden ayah Olwen, dibunuh Goreu fab Custennin.
claims.quote: Ysbaddaden, chief of giants, is the father of Olwen, a beautiful maiden sought by Culhwch fab Cilydd, a cousin of King Arthur's. He is slain at the tale's close by his nephew Goreu fab Custennin

claims.statement: Rhitta Gawr: a cape of kings' beards; demanded Arthur's beard.
claims.statement_id: Rhitta Gawr: jubah dari janggut raja-raja; menuntut janggut Arthur.
claims.quote: The twenty-six kings of Britain assembled their armies to destroy Rhitta but were vanquished by the giant, who cut off the kings' beards and fashioned a great cape out of them to protect him from the cold.

claims.statement: cy article: giants (cewri) appear regularly in Welsh folklore and myth.
claims.statement_id: Artikel cy: raksasa (cewri) sering muncul dalam folklor dan mitologi Welsh.
claims.quote: Mae cewri yn ymddangos yn rheolaidd yn llên gwerin a mytholeg Cymraeg.

claims.statement: Gwragedd Annwn (gwraig Annwn; Dames of Elfin Land, Wives of the Lower World, Lake Maidens), female fairies beneath lakes and rivers in Welsh folklore; Tylwyth Teg.
claims.statement_id: Gwragedd Annwn (gwraig Annwn; Dames of Elfin Land, Wives of the Lower World, Lake Maidens), peri perempuan di bawah danau dan sungai folklor Welsh (Wales); Tylwyth Teg.
claims.quote: alternatively known as Dames of the Lower Region, Dames of Elfin Land, or Wives of the Lower World, are beautiful female fairies who live beneath lakes and rivers found in Welsh folklore. They are counted among the Tylwyth Teg or Welsh fairy folk.

claims.statement: Tied to the origin of Welsh black cattle; sometimes visible in the upper world.
claims.statement_id: Terkait asal sapi hitam Welsh; kadang terlihat di dunia atas.
claims.quote: The mythological narrative of Gwragedd Annwn is intertwined with the origin of the Welsh black cattle. Occasionally, the fairies were said to ascend into the upper world, and be visible to ordinary people.

claims.statement: St. Patrick (from Ireland to Wales to meet St. David) turned his abusers into fish; the women into lake fairies.
claims.statement_id: St. Patrick (dari Irlandia ke Wales menemui St. David) mengubah pencacinya menjadi ikan; perempuan menjadi peri danau.
claims.quote: St. Patrick, who was Welsh and therefore could understand their insults, punished the offending Welsh folk by transforming them into fish. However, since some of the people there were women, they were instead transformed into Lake Fairies.

claims.statement: Llyn Barfog, Gwynedd; Crumlyn Lake near Briton Ferry; unlike selkies or merrows.
claims.statement_id: Llyn Barfog, Gwynedd; Danau Crumlyn (Crumlyn Lake) dekat Briton Ferry; tak seperti selkie atau merrow.
claims.quote: notably the "Bearded Lake" Llyn Barfog in Gwynedd and Crumlyn Lake, located near Briton Ferry, Neath Port Talbot, Wales.

claims.statement: The Gwragedd Annwn dressed in green.
claims.statement_id: Gwragedd Annwn berpakaian hijau.
claims.quote: The Gwragedd Annwn dressed in green.

claims.statement: fr article: Gwagged annwn, a Welsh lake fairy, symbol of the eternal quest for love.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: Gwagged annwn, peri danau Wales, melambangkan pencarian cinta abadi.
claims.quote: Gwagged annwn est une fée lacustre du Pays de Galles, qui représente la quête éternelle de l'amour.

claims.statement: Hob, small household spirit of the English Midlands, Northern England, Anglo-Scottish border; works on farms; driven off by new clothes.
claims.statement_id: Hob, roh rumah kecil Midlands Inggris (English), Inggris Utara (Northern England), perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish); bekerja di pertanian; diusir dengan pakaian baru.
claims.quote: A hob is a type of small mythological household spirit found in the English Midlands, Northern England, and on the Anglo-Scottish border, according to traditional folklore of those regions. They could live inside the house or outdoors. They are said to work in farmyards and thus could be helpful; however if offended they could become nuisances.

claims.statement: Cognate with the brownie, nisse, tomte; from the cofgodas, old English house-gods.
claims.statement_id: Berkerabat dengan brownie, nisse, tomte; dari cofgodas (dewa rumah kuno Inggris).
claims.quote: As well as the brownie, another cognate exists in the Scandinavian nisse or tomte; all are thought to be derived from the household gods of olden times, known in England as the cofgodas

claims.statement: Hob, diminutive of Robin and Robert; generic for goblin, bogle, brownie; Old English þyrs, Old Norse þurs; hob-thrush, hob-thrust.
claims.statement_id: Hob bentuk kecil Robin dan Robert; istilah umum goblin, bogle, brownie; þyrs (Inggris Kuno), þurs (Norse Kuno); hob-thrush, hob-thrust.
claims.quote: ‘Hob’ is a diminutive form of the name Robin, which is itself a diminutive form of the name Robert. Hob is sometimes a generic term given to a goblin, bogle or brownie.

claims.statement: The Runswick Bay hob in a hobhole cured whooping cough.
claims.statement_id: Hob Runswick Bay di hobhole menyembuhkan batuk rejan.
claims.quote: One famous hob lived near Runswick Bay in a hobhole; this hob was believed to be able to cure young children of kink-cough (whooping cough).

claims.statement: Yorkshire: small, hairy, wizened men; kind but mischievous; about at night.
claims.statement_id: Yorkshire: lelaki kecil berbulu, keriput; baik tetapi nakal; aktif malam.
claims.quote: Hobs have been described as small, hairy, wizened men. Hobs were viewed as kind but mischievous spirits, helpful to local people in need.

claims.statement: fy article: the hob, a mythical being of English folklore.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fy: hob, makhluk mitos folklor Inggris (Ingelân).
claims.quote: In hob is in mytysk wêzen út 'e folkloare fan Ingelân.

claims.statement: Hobs were disposed of by giving new clothes; they left forever.
claims.statement_id: Hob diusir dengan diberi pakaian baru; pergi selamanya.
claims.quote: The usual way to dispose of hobs was to give them a set of new clothing, the receiving of which would make the creatures leave forever.

claims.statement: Lantern man, a ghost light of the Fens of East Anglia, England; Wicken Fen; L. F. Newman; evil spirits luring to reed beds.
claims.statement_id: Lantern man, cahaya hantu folklor The Fens, East Anglia, Inggris (England); Wicken Fen; L. F. Newman (L.F. Newman); roh jahat ke rawa alang-alang.
claims.quote: A lantern man is an atmospheric ghost light described in the folklore of The Fens of East Anglia, with sightings around Wicken Fen and other areas. According to the stories, first collected by folklorist L.F. Newman, the lights are believed to be evil spirits who attempt to draw victims to their death in the reed beds.

claims.statement: Attracted by whistling; evade by lying face down, mouth in the mud.
claims.statement_id: Tertarik siulan; hindari dengan berbaring telungkup, mulut di lumpur.
claims.quote: Newman writes that the spirits are attracted by the sound of whistling, and that a way to evade them is to lie face down on the ground with your mouth in the mud.

claims.statement: A will-o'-the-wisp variant; now dismissed as marsh gas.
claims.statement_id: Variasi will-o'-the-wisp; kini dianggap gas rawa.
claims.quote: The phenomenon, which seems to be a variation of will-o'-the-wisp folklore, is now dismissed as sightings of combustible marsh gas.

claims.statement: A fisherman to Peter Underwood; a horn on a pole burnt up.
claims.statement_id: Nelayan kepada Peter Underwood; tanduk pada tiang hangus terbakar.
claims.quote: A local fisherman recounted to parapsychologist Peter Underwood how he had once thrown himself to the floor to escape the attention of a lantern man which had been drawn to his whistling.

claims.statement: zh article: per L. F. Newman, the lights are evil spirits luring victims to the reeds.
claims.statement_id: Artikel zh: menurut L. F. Newman, cahaya itu roh jahat yang menarik korban ke alang-alang.
claims.quote: 根据民俗学家 l.f. 纽曼收集的故事中， 这些怪火被认为是邪灵作祟，以试图吸引受害者前往芦苇丛。

claims.statement: A man who had taken shelter at a friend's home was helped when the friend hung out a horn on a long pole to distract the spirit, and the following morning the horn was found burnt up.
claims.statement_id: Seorang lelaki yang berlindung di rumah temannya diselamatkan ketika sang teman menggantungkan sebuah tanduk pada tiang panjang untuk mengalihkan roh itu, dan keesokan paginya tanduk itu ditemukan hangus terbakar.
claims.quote: The man had taken shelter at the home of a friend, who hung out a horn on a long pole to distract the spirit. The following morning the horn was found to have been burnt up.

claims.statement: Lí Ban (Liban; Old Irish lí beauty + ban of women), a woman turned mermaid, legend of Lough Neagh, Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Lí Ban (Liban; lí kecantikan + ban perempuan, Irlandia Kuno), perempuan menjadi putri duyung, legenda Lough Neagh, Irlandia.
claims.quote: in the legend surrounding the formation of Lough Neagh, was a woman turned mermaid who inhabited the area before the great lake gushed up on dry land.

claims.statement: Family drowned; a year in an underwater chamber; became half human, half salmon.
claims.statement_id: Keluarga tenggelam; setahun di ruang bawah air; menjadi setengah manusia setengah salem.
claims.quote: Her family was drowned, but she survived in an underwater chamber in the lake for a year, after which she was transformed into a being who was half-human, half-salmon.

claims.statement: Baptised by St. Comgall: Muirgein/Muirgeilt; Saint Muirgen, 27 January; messenger to Rome; Inbhear nOllarbha (Larne Lough).
claims.statement_id: Dibaptis Comgall (St. Comgall): Muirgein/Muirgeilt; Santo (Saint) Muirgen, 27 Januari (January); utusan ke Roma (Rome); Inbhear nOllarbha (Larne Lough).
claims.quote: There she was baptised by Comgall, and given the Christened name Muirgein ("sea-born") or Muirgeilt ("sea-wander") . She appears as Saint Muirgen in genealogies of Irish saints with her feast day assigned to 27 January.

claims.statement: Annals of the Four Masters: captured 558 AD.
claims.statement_id: Annals of the Four Masters: ditangkap 558 M (A.D.).
claims.quote: Liban, a mermaid (muirgelt) who was the daughter of Eochaid, was captured in the year 558 A.D. according to the Annals of the Four Masters

claims.statement: Aided Echach maic Maireda, 12th-century Lebor na hUidre; Lough Neagh named after her father Eochaid mac Mairidh.
claims.statement_id: Aided Echach maic Maireda, Lebor na hUidre abad ke-12; Lough Neagh dinamai menurut ayahnya Eochaid mac Mairidh.
claims.quote: According to this old tale, Liban turned into a mermaid when a spring burst under her house to form Lough Neagh (Old Irish: Loch nEchach ), named after Liban's father Eochaid mac Mairidh who was drowned by the gushing water.

claims.statement: fi article: Liban chose heaven, was baptised and died.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fi: Liban memilih surga, dibaptis, lalu meninggal.
claims.quote: Liban valitsi taivaan, otti kasteen ja kuoli.

claims.statement: Maggy Moulach (Meg Mullach, Maggie Moloch, Maug Moulach, Hairy Meg), a Highland brownie of Scottish folklore; son Brownie-Clod, a dobie.
claims.statement_id: Maggy Moulach (Meg Mullach, Maggie Moloch, Maug Moulach, Hairy Meg), brownie Dataran Tinggi (Highland) folklor Skotlandia (Scottish); putra Brownie-Clod, dobie.
claims.quote: is a character from Scottish folklore said to be a Highland brownie. According to the folklore, she had a son named Brownie-Clod, who was said to be a dobie. A dobie is a somewhat dull-witted, though well-intentioned, variety of brownie.

claims.statement: Two feet tall, thick hair or hairy hands, Hairy Meg; turns into a grasshopper.
claims.statement_id: Setinggi dua kaki, rambut lebat atau tangan berbulu, Hairy Meg; berubah menjadi belalang.
claims.quote: She is described as a 2 ft 0 in (0.61 m) tall creature with an impressive head of hair or (and), as said in other lore, with hairy hands; that is why she was sometimes called Hairy Meg.

claims.statement: Tullochgorm castle of the Grant family; helped win at chess; family banshee.
claims.statement_id: Kastel Tullochgorm milik keluarga Grant; membantu menang catur; banshee keluarga.
claims.quote: In the earlier legends, it is said that Meg and her son were living in Tullochgorm castle, which belonged to the Grant family. She performed the usual labors of brownie, but also helped the clan chief beat his opponents at chess.

claims.statement: The girl called herself Mi fein (me myself) and scalded Brownie-Clod.
claims.statement_id: Gadis mengaku bernama Mi fein (diriku sendiri) dan menyiram Brownie-Clod dengan air mendidih.
claims.quote: Keeping his distance, he asked for her name and the quick girl replied, "Oh, I'm Mise mi fein" which means "Oh, I am me myself".

claims.statement: Maggy took revenge, hurling a stool that killed the girl.
claims.statement_id: Maggy membalas dendam dengan melempar bangku hingga gadis tewas.
claims.quote: Maggy overhears the girl one day while walking past her window and takes vengeance. She throws a stool with such force that it kills the girl dead on the spot.

claims.statement: sco article: in later versions of the story she raxed doun lums and choled bairns (reached down chimneys, stole children); able to shapeshift into a grasshopper.
claims.statement_id: Artikel sco: versi kemudian, ia menjulurkan tangan lewat cerobong (raxed doun lums) mencuri anak (choled bairns); dapat shapeshift menjadi belalang (grasshopper).
claims.quote: In some later versions o the story, it is said thit she raxed doun lums an choled bairns. She wis able tae shapeshift intae a grasshopper an aw.

claims.statement: Mooinjer veggey, Manx for little people (fairies) in Gaelic lore; Irish Muintir Bheaga, Scottish Gaelic Muinntir Bheaga; Isle of Man.
claims.statement_id: Mooinjer veggey, bahasa Manx untuk orang kecil (peri) dalam tradisi Gaelik (Gaelic); Irlandia (Irish) Muintir Bheaga, Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic) Muinntir Bheaga; Pulau Man.
claims.quote: Mooinjer veggey is the Manx for little people, a term used for fairies in Gaelic lore. The equivalent Irish and Scottish Gaelic are Muintir Bheaga and Muinntir Bheaga .

claims.statement: 2–3 ft tall, red caps, green jackets, on horseback with rainbow-coloured hounds; mischievous and spiteful.
claims.statement_id: Setinggi 2–3 kaki, topi merah, jaket hijau, menunggang kuda dengan anjing kecil warna pelangi; nakal dan pendendam.
claims.quote: In Manx folklore, the mooinjer veggey are small creatures ranging 2–3 ft (0.61–0.91 m) in height, otherwise very like mortals. They wear red caps and green jackets and are most often seen on horseback followed by packs of little hounds of all the colours of the rainbow. They are rather inclined to be mischievous and spiteful.

claims.statement: Live on green hillsides and ancient tumuli; delightful music on summer evenings.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di lereng hijau dan gundukan kubur kuno; musik indah malam musim panas.
claims.quote: They live in green hillsides, more especially ancient tumuli. Anyone straying near these on a fine summer's evening would probably hear delightful music

claims.statement: Visible only when they choose; some heal, some steal children.
claims.statement_id: Terlihat hanya bila mau; sebagian menyembuhkan, sebagian mencuri anak.
claims.quote: They are visible to people only when they choose. Some of them are benevolent, curing men of diseases and delivering them from misfortune. Others are malevolent, stealing children, even abducting adults, and bringing misfortune.

claims.statement: Manxwomen did not spin on Saturday evenings; fire, bread, water for them; salt and iron against evil charms.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan Manx (Manxwomen) tak memintal Sabtu malam; api, roti, air untuk mereka; garam dan besi melawan pesona jahat.
claims.quote: Manxwomen would not spin on Saturday evenings, as this was deemed displeasing to the mooinjer veggey , and at every baking and churning a small piece of dough and butter was stuck on the wall for their consumption. Both salt and iron were considered efficacious against malevolent charms.

claims.statement: cy article: small beings two to three feet tall, like mortals.
claims.statement_id: Artikel cy: makhluk kecil setinggi dua sampai tiga kaki, mirip manusia.
claims.quote: Yn llên gwerin Manaweg,  mae'r Mooinjer veggey yn greaduriaid bach o ddwy i dair troedfedd (600 i 900 mm) o uchder, fel arall yn debyg iawn i feidrolion.

claims.statement: Muc-sheilche (Muc-sheilch), a lake monster of Scottish folklore in Loch Maree; means turtle-pig.
claims.statement_id: Muc-sheilche (Muc-sheilch), monster danau folklor Skotlandia (Scottish), di Loch Maree; berarti babi-penyu.
claims.quote: is a lake monster said to live in Loch Maree, and its neighbouring lochs. The term loosely translates as "turtle-pig."

claims.statement: ga article (Irish muc thurtair): lives in Loch Ma-Ruibhe and nearby lochs.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ga (muc thurtair, Irlandia): tinggal di Loch Ma-Ruibhe dan danau sekitarnya.
claims.quote: Deirtear go bhfuil sí ina cónaí i Loch Ma-Ruibhe, agus sna lochanna sa cheantar máguaird.

claims.statement: Like Loch Ness and Loch Morar, Loch Maree is said to have its own monster in the form of the muc-sheilch.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Loch Ness dan Loch Morar, Loch Maree disebut memiliki monsternya sendiri berupa muc-sheilch.
claims.quote: Like Loch Ness and Loch Morar, Loch Maree has its own monster in the form of the muc-sheilch.

claims.statement: Loch Maree is a loch in Wester Ross in the Northwest Highlands of Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Loch Maree adalah sebuah loch di Wester Ross, Dataran Tinggi Barat Laut Skotlandia.
claims.quote: is a loch in Wester Ross in the Northwest Highlands of Scotland.

claims.statement: Loch Maree is the fourth-largest freshwater loch in Scotland and the largest north of Loch Ness.
claims.statement_id: Loch Maree adalah loch air tawar terbesar keempat di Skotlandia dan yang terbesar di sebelah utara Loch Ness.
claims.quote: it is the fourth-largest freshwater loch in Scotland; it is the largest north of Loch Ness.

claims.statement: Thomas Pennant, writing in 1772, recorded that the loch was considered a holy well whose waters were thought to have curative effects.
claims.statement_id: Thomas Pennant, menulis pada 1772, mencatat bahwa loch itu dianggap sumur suci yang airnya diyakini berkhasiat menyembuhkan.
claims.quote: Thomas Pennant, writing in 1772, recorded that the loch was considered a holy well whose waters were thought to have curative effects

claims.statement: Pillywiggins, tiny goblins and fairies guarding flora, English and Irish folklore; butterfly or dragonfly wings; in groups among flowers.
claims.statement_id: Pillywiggin, goblin dan peri mungil penjaga tumbuhan, folklor Inggris (English) dan Irlandia (Irish); sayap kupu-kupu atau capung; berkelompok di antara bunga.
claims.quote: Pillywiggins are tiny goblins and fairies, guardians of the flora, mentioned in English and Irish folklore. Tiny in size, they have the antennae and wings of a butterfly or dragonfly, live in groups and spend their time frolicking among the flowers.

claims.statement: Linked to spring flowers; the divine essence of plants.
claims.statement_id: Terkait bunga musim semi; esensi ilahi tumbuhan.
claims.quote: Pillywiggins are fairies from English folklore, associated with spring flowers and personifying the "divine essence of plants".

claims.statement: The name Pillywiggin appeared in 1977 in Nancy Arrowsmith's Field Guide to the Little People; from Dorset.
claims.statement_id: Nama Pillywiggin muncul 1977 dalam Field Guide to the Little People karya Nancy Arrowsmith; dari Dorset.
claims.quote: The name "Pillywiggin" appeared in 1977 in the American Nancy Arrowsmith's Field Guide to the Little People, who believes that the name of these creatures comes from the English county of Dorset.

claims.statement: Winged, a centimetre long, can change size; eat dew and pollen; join weddings; no tricks on humans.
claims.statement_id: Bersayap, satu sentimeter, dapat berubah ukuran; makan embun dan serbuk sari; ikut pesta pernikahan; tidak mengerjai manusia.
claims.quote: Winged, they usually measure a centimetre, but can change size. Their food consists of dew and pollen. They are trooping fairies, creatures that live in groups.

claims.statement: Edain McCoy (1994): pillywiggin queen Ariel rides bats.
claims.statement_id: Edain McCoy (1994): ratu pillywiggin Ariel menunggang kelelawar.
claims.quote: describing a very seductive pillywiggins queen, who goes by the name of Ariel and rides bats.

claims.statement: fr article: tiny lutins and fairies guarding flora, English and Irish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: lutin dan peri mungil penjaga tumbuhan, folklor Inggris dan Irlandia.
claims.quote: Les pillywiggins sont de minuscules lutins et fées gardiens de la flore, cités par le folklore anglais et irlandais.

claims.statement: Seelie (Seely), Scots for happy, lucky, blessed; fairies of Scottish folklore; seely wights, Seelie Court; ambivalent, dangerous.
claims.statement_id: Seelie (Seely), istilah Skots (Scots): bahagia, beruntung, diberkati; peri folklor Skotlandia (Scottish); seely wights, Seelie Court; ambivalen, berbahaya.
claims.quote: Seelie (or Seely) is from the Scots term seelie meaning "happy", "lucky" or "blessed" applied to fairy beings in Scottish folklore in phrases such as seely wights or The Seelie Court. Despite their name, the seelie folk of legend could be morally ambivalent and dangerous.

claims.statement: A euphemism like good neighbours to avoid their anger.
claims.statement_id: Eufemisme seperti tetangga baik untuk menghindari amarah.
claims.quote: Calling them "seelie," similar to names such as "good neighbors," may have been a euphemism to ward off their anger.

claims.statement: From Old Scots sele, good fortune; modern English silly descends from seely.
claims.statement_id: Dari Skots Kuno (Old Scots) sele, keberuntungan; kata Inggris (English) modern silly berasal dari seely.
claims.quote: The word seely (var. seily , seelie , sealy ) is the adjective form of Scots language sele, seel , from Old Scots sele 'good fortune, bliss'

claims.statement: William Hay, 16th century: celly vichtys; Seilie wichts; Julian Goodare: nature spirits.
claims.statement_id: William Hay abad ke-16: celly vichtys; Seilie wichts; Julian Goodare: roh alam.
claims.quote: One of the earliest pieces of evidence comes from the sixteenth-century theologian William Hay, who complained of witches and local pagans claiming to meet with fairy-like women called "celly vichtys."

claims.statement: Seelie Court good fairies, opposed to the Unseelie Court; Katharine Mary Briggs: seek help, repay kindness, avenge insults.
claims.statement_id: Seelie Court peri baik, lawan Unseelie Court; Katharine Mary Briggs: meminta bantuan, membalas kebaikan, membalas penghinaan.
claims.quote: The Seelie Court is a group of fairies, often specified as good fairies who contrast with the wicked Unseelie Court. As described by British folklorist Katharine Mary Briggs, the Seelie Court were those fairies who would seek help from humans, warn those who have accidentally offended them, and return human kindness with favors of their own.

claims.statement: cs article: appear at dusk in elegant processions; harshly avenge insults.
claims.statement_id: Artikel cs: muncul saat senja dalam arak-arakan anggun; membalas penghinaan dengan keras.
claims.quote: Často se objevují za soumraku v elegantních průvodech a přes svou mírnou povahu se tvrdě mstí za křivdy a urážky.

claims.statement: Shellycoat (spellycoat), a prankster water spirit of Scottish and Northern English folklore; rivers; east coast.
claims.statement_id: Shellycoat (spellycoat), roh air jahil folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Scotland) dan Inggris Utara (Northern English); sungai; pesisir timur.
claims.quote: In Scottish and Northern English folklore, a shellycoat (also called spellycoat) is a prankster water spirit that haunts rivers and streams. They are mainly described on the east coast of Scotland.

claims.statement: Long hair, webbed feet, covered in clattering shells; like a tangie.
claims.statement_id: Bulu panjang, kaki berselaput, tertutup cangkang yang berderak; mirip tangie.
claims.quote: The shellycoat is said to have long hair all over its body, along with webbed feet. The hair is covered in shells and other ocean debris, making a clattering sound as it moves. They are similar to a tangie, which is covered in seaweed.

claims.statement: Harmless compared to the kelpie; misleads without malice; cries as if drowning, laughs like a horse.
claims.statement_id: Tak berbahaya dibanding kelpie; menyesatkan tanpa niat jahat; berteriak seperti tenggelam lalu tertawa seperti kuda.
claims.quote: Shellycoats are considered to be relatively harmless compared to other water spirits like the kelpie. They may mislead wanderers, particularly those they think are trespassing upon the creature's territory, but without malice. A common tactic of a shellycoat would be to cry out as if drowning and then laugh like a horse at the distracted victim.

claims.statement: Cannot cross running water; leaves women with children alone.
claims.statement_id: Tak dapat menyeberangi air mengalir; membiarkan perempuan beranak.
claims.quote: It is believed that the shellycoat cannot cross running water and that it leaves women with children alone.

claims.statement: Shellycoat of Leith: large evil spirit, could fly; English Dick; rock destroyed early 1900s.
claims.statement_id: Shellycoat dari (of) Leith: roh jahat besar, dapat terbang; English Dick; batu hancur awal 1900-an.
claims.quote: The shellycoat of Leith was described as a large, evil spirit that was capable of flight. He would hide his magic coat of shells under a rock when not wearing it, during which times he was harmless.

claims.statement: Jacob Grimm, Deutsche Mythologie: same as the German Schellenrock, bell-coat.
claims.statement_id: Jacob Grimm, Deutsche Mythologie: sama dengan Schellenrock Jerman (German), mantel lonceng.
claims.quote: Jacob Grimm stated in his Deutsche Mythologie that the Scottish goblin Shellycoat is one and the same as the German Schellenrock, that is bell-coat

claims.statement: de article: the clatter of shells reveals its presence.
claims.statement_id: Artikel de: derak cangkang menandakan kehadirannya.
claims.quote: Das Klappern der Muscheln verrät dem aufmerksamen Wanderer seine Anwesenheit.

claims.statement: Stoor worm (Mester Stoor Worm), a giant evil sea serpent of Orcadian folklore, Scotland; putrid breath; variant of the Norse Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent; a sea dragon.
claims.statement_id: Stoor worm (Mester Stoor Worm), ular laut raksasa jahat folklor Orkney (Orcadian), Skotlandia; napas busuk; varian Jörmungandr Norse, Ular Midgard (Midgard Serpent); naga laut.
claims.quote: The stoor worm, or Mester Stoor Worm, was a gigantic evil sea serpent of Orcadian folklore, capable of contaminating plants and destroying animals and humans with its putrid breath. It is probably an Orkney variant of the Norse Jörmungandr, also known as the Midgard Serpent, or world serpent, and has been described as a sea dragon.

claims.statement: Assipattle defeated it; teeth became Orkney, Shetland, the Faroes; body became Iceland.
claims.statement_id: Assipattle mengalahkannya; gigi menjadi Kepulauan Orkney, Shetland, Faroe; tubuh menjadi Islandia (Iceland).
claims.quote: Assipattle, the youngest son of a local farmer, defeated the creature; as it died its teeth fell out to become the islands of Orkney, Shetland and the Faroes, and its body became Iceland.

claims.statement: Name from Old Norse Storðar-gandr, another name for Jörmungandr.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Norse Kuno (Old Norse) Storðar-gandr, nama lain Jörmungandr.
claims.quote: The name stoor worm may be derived from the Old Norse Storðar-gandr, an alternative name for Jörmungandr, the world or Midgard Serpent of Norse mythology

claims.statement: Mester means master; master and father of all stoorworms.
claims.statement_id: Mester berarti tuan; tuan dan bapak semua stoorworm.
claims.quote: Mester means master; it may have been deemed Mester Stoor Worm because it was the "master and father of all stoorworms".

claims.statement: The king offered seven virgins weekly; offered kingdom, daughter, magic sword.
claims.statement_id: Raja mempersembahkan tujuh perawan seminggu; menawarkan kerajaan, putri, pedang ajaib.
claims.quote: The king of one country threatened by the beast's arrival was advised to offer it a weekly sacrifice of seven virgins.

claims.statement: sr article: a giant evil Orkney sea serpent with putrid breath.
claims.statement_id: Artikel sr: ular laut raksasa jahat Orkney dengan napas busuk.
claims.quote: Стур црв, или Местер Стур Црв, била је огромна зла морска змија из орканијског фолклора, способна да контаминира биљке и уништи животиње и људе својим трулим дахом.

claims.statement: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh (of Bamborough), a Northumbrian ballad; a princess turned into a dragon.
claims.statement_id: Laidly Worm dari (of) Spindleston Heugh (The Laidly Worm of Bamborough), balada Northumbria (Northumbrian); putri diubah menjadi naga.
claims.quote: The Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh, also known as The Laidly Worm of Bamborough, is a Northumbrian ballad about a princess who is changed into a dragon (the "laidly worm" of the title).

claims.statement: Kingdom of Northumbria, Bamburgh Castle; the witch, jealous of Princess Margaret, turns her into a dragon; Childe Wynd overseas.
claims.statement_id: Kerajaan (Kingdom of) Northumbria, Kastel (Castle) Bamburgh; penyihir iri pada Putri (Princess) Margaret mengubahnya jadi naga; Childe Wynd di seberang laut.
claims.quote: The King's son, Childe Wynd, has gone across the sea and the witch, jealous of the beauty of the king’s daughter, Princess Margaret, and quick to take advantage of Wynd’s absence, turns her into a dragon.

claims.statement: The prince kisses the dragon thrice, the princess restored; the witch-queen made a toad.
claims.statement_id: Pangeran mencium naga tiga kali, putri pulih; ratu penyihir menjadi katak.
claims.quote: Later in the story, the prince returns and, instead of fighting the dragon, kisses it, restoring the princess to her natural form. He then turns the witch-queen into a toad and becomes king.

claims.statement: First published 1778; Reverend Robert Lambe; Latin manuscript of 1270; thought a forgery.
claims.statement_id: Diterbitkan pertama 1778; Pendeta Robert Lambe; naskah Latin 1270; dianggap pemalsuan.
claims.quote: The ballad was first published in 1778 in a compilation of folk songs.

claims.statement: Joseph Jacobs's version: seven cows a day.
claims.statement_id: Versi Joseph Jacobs: tujuh sapi per hari.
claims.quote: In Joseph Jacob's version, the dragon Princess Margaret is appeased by putting aside seven cows for her per day.

claims.statement: ja article: the king at Bamburgh Castle in the Kingdom of Northumbria brought home a new queen.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ja: raja di Kastel Bamburgh (Bamburgh Castle), Kerajaan Northumbria, membawa pulang ratu baru.
claims.quote: ある日七王国時代の国の1つであるノーサンブリア王国のバンバラ城（Bamburgh Castle）の王が新しい后（女王）を連れて戻ってきた。

claims.statement: The Ratman of Southend, an English urban legend from Southend-on-Sea, Essex.
claims.statement_id: Ratman dari (of) Southend, legenda urban Inggris (English), Southend-on-Sea, Essex.
claims.quote: The Ratman of Southend is an English urban legend originating in Southend-on-Sea, Essex.

claims.statement: A homeless man beaten in the underpass; his face eaten by vermin.
claims.statement_id: Lelaki tunawisma dipukuli di terowongan; wajahnya dimakan binatang pengerat.
claims.quote: As he died, the numerous vermin who inhabit the area gathered, and were found to have devoured his face.

claims.statement: A ghostly figure in the underpass; rat-like squeals and claw scraping.
claims.statement_id: Sosok hantu di terowongan; cicitan tikus dan garukan cakar di dinding.
claims.quote: After this, a ghostly figure was spotted in the underpass, with people hearing ratlike squealing, and scraping, as if large claws were moving across the walls.

claims.statement: Short film by Michael Holiday, Horror-on-Sea festival 2019.
claims.statement_id: Film pendek Michael Holiday, festival Horror-on-Sea 2019.
claims.quote: A short film about the Ratman of Southend, directed by Michael Holiday, was entered in 2019 during the annual Horror-on-Sea film festival in Southend.

claims.statement: Enemy in Fallout: London (2024).
claims.statement_id: Musuh dalam Fallout: London (2024).
claims.quote: The Ratman of Southend appears as an enemy in the quest Anglicans and Demons in the 2024 mod for Fallout 4, Fallout: London.

claims.statement: vi article: an English urban legend from Southend-on-Sea, Essex.
claims.statement_id: Artikel vi: legenda urban Inggris dari Southend-on-Sea, Essex.
claims.quote: Người chuột Southend (tiếng Anh: The Ratman of Southend) là truyền thuyết thành thị nước Anh bắt nguồn từ Southend-on-Sea, Essex.

claims.statement: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), lutin-like, Lower Brittany folklore; island of Ushant; François-Marie Luzel; Breton.
claims.statement_id: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), mirip lutin, folklor Basse-Bretagne (Lower Brittany, Prancis); Pulau Ouessant (Ushant); François-Marie Luzel; Breton.
claims.quote: The Tréo-Fall, also known as danserien-noz, are lutin-like creatures from the folklore of Lower Brittany. Under this first name, they are specific to the island of Ushant, where traditions about them were collected by François-Marie Luzel.

claims.statement: Dance on clifftops by moonlight, promising treasure; Plouaret, January 1869.
claims.statement_id: Menari di puncak tebing di bawah bulan, menjanjikan harta; Plouaret, Januari (January) 1869.
claims.quote: The Tréo-Fall are said to gather at the top of cliffs to dance in the moonlight, promising treasures to humans who cross their path. Two tales about "night dancers" were collected in Plouaret in January 1869.

claims.statement: A knife in the ground touched each round; wish granted; dancers often break kidneys; Paul Sébillot: small size.
claims.statement_id: Pisau di tanah disentuh tiap putaran; permintaan dikabulkan; penari sering ginjal rusak; Paul Sébillot: tubuh kecil.
claims.quote: The only way to escape is to stick a knife in the ground, then graze it at each dance circle. If the dancer succeeds in fulfilling this condition, the Tréo-Fall will grant his or her request, whatever it may be.

claims.statement: François-Marie Luzel and Françoise Morvan: a kind of Korrigan; the knife on Ouessant; night dancer (danseur de nuit); reward and punishment.
claims.statement_id: François-Marie Luzel dan Françoise Morvan: jenis Korrigan; pisau di Ouessant; penari malam (danseur de nuit); hadiah dan hukuman.
claims.quote: François-Marie Luzel and Françoise Morvan see the Tréo-Fall as a particular variety of Korrigans, linked to a local use of the knife on the island of Ouessant.

claims.statement: fr article: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), lutin-like, Basse-Bretagne.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), mirip lutin, Basse-Bretagne.
claims.quote: Les Tréo-Fall, également connus sous le nom de danserien-noz, sont des créatures du folklore populaire de la Basse-Bretagne, de type lutin.

claims.statement: Luzel writes that there are also the treo-fall, or evil spirits, called elsewhere ann danserienn noz, the night dancers.
claims.statement_id: Luzel menulis bahwa ada pula treo-fall, atau roh jahat, yang di tempat lain juga disebut ann danserienn noz, para penari malam.
claims.quote: Il y a encore les treo-fall ou mauvais esprits, appelés aussi ailleurs ann danserienn noz, les danseurs de nuit.

claims.statement: According to Luzel, they lead their fantastic rounds by moonlight on the seashore or atop the cliffs and invite passers-by to join in by promising treasures.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Luzel, mereka menari dalam lingkaran fantastis di bawah cahaya bulan, di tepi laut atau di puncak tebing, dan mengajak para pejalan kaki ikut serta dengan menjanjikan harta.
claims.quote: Ils mènent leurs rondes fantastiques, au clair de la lune, sur le rivage de la mer ou au haut des falaises, et invitent les passants à y prendre part en leur promettant des trésors.

claims.statement: The man who accepts must plant his knife in the ground, then follow the round, spinning as fast as a whirlwind, and graze the knife on each turn without ever passing it; otherwise his back is broken and he is left dying on the spot.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang menerima harus menancapkan pisaunya di tanah, lalu mengikuti lingkaran dengan putaran secepat pusaran dan menyentuh pisau itu setiap putaran tanpa pernah melewatinya; bila tidak, punggungnya dipatahkan dan ia ditinggalkan sekarat di tempat.
claims.quote: L’homme qui accepte doit planter son couteau en terre, puis, en suivant la ronde et en tournant avec la rapidité d’un tourbillon, il faut qu’il le rase à chaque tour, sans jamais le dépasser, autrement on lui rompt les reins et on le laisse mourant sur la place.

claims.statement: Ysgithyrwyn (Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd, Ysgithrwyn Pen Beidd), White-tusk chief of Boars, hunted by Arthur's party in Culhwch ac Olwen, Welsh; Twrch Trwyth.
claims.statement_id: Ysgithyrwyn (Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd, Ysgithrwyn Pen Beidd), Si Taring Putih kepala babi hutan, diburu rombongan Arthur dalam Culhwch ac Olwen, Welsh (Wales); Twrch Trwyth.
claims.quote: or "White-tusk chief of Boars" is another boar being hunted, secondary to the great boar Twrch Trwyth by the Arthur's wild chase party in the Welsh Arthurian romance Culhwch ac Olwen.

claims.statement: Tusk (ysgithyr) to shave Ysbaddaden; pulled alive; Odgar son of Aedd, king of Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Taring (ysgithyr) untuk mencukur Ysbaddaden; dicabut hidup-hidup; Odgar putra (son of) Aedd raja Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: Its tusk (Welsh: ysgithyr ) was the necessary implement for shaving the giant Ysbaddaden Chief-Giant. Ysbaddaden proclaimed this tusk was no use to him unless extracted from the boar while still alive, and only Odgar the son of Aedd the king of Ireland was capable of accomplishing this.

claims.statement: Slain by Cavall, Arthur's own dog.
claims.statement_id: Dibunuh oleh Cavall, anjing Arthur.
claims.quote: This boar was slain (or at least chased down and cornered into inevitable death) not "by the dogs that Yspaddaden had mentioned, but by Cavall, Arthur's own dog.".

claims.statement: Kaw of North Britain, on Llamrei, split the boar's head with an axe; took the tusk per Arthur's vow.
claims.statement_id: Kaw dari Britania Utara (North Britain), menunggang Llamrei, membelah kepala babi dengan kapak; mengambil taring sesuai sumpah Arthur.
claims.quote: In fact it was Kaw of North Britain (Cadw of Pydein, or Pictland), who, mounted on Arthur's mare Llamrei swung a battle-axe or hatchet (Welsh: bwyellic, bwyellig ) at the boar and spliced its head.

claims.statement: de article: a mythical boar of Welsh myth in the King Arthur cycle; Weißhauer (white tusk).
claims.statement_id: Artikel de: babi hutan mitos mitologi Welsh dalam siklus Raja Arthur; Weißhauer (taring putih).
claims.quote: Ysgithyrwyn Penbaedd [ ɘsgi'θɘruin 'penbaið] („Weißhauer der oberste Eber“), walisisch Ysgithrwyn Pen Beidd, Yskithyrwynn Pennbeidd; mittelwalisische yskithyrwyn penn beird, ist der Name eines mythischen Ebers in der Walisischen Mythologie im Sagenkreis um König Arthur.

claims.statement: Lady Guest's translation: Ysbaddaden needs the tusk of Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd, plucked alive; Arthur leads his dog Cavall.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Lady Guest: Ysbaddaden membutuhkan taring Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd, dicabut hidup-hidup; Arthur memimpin anjingnya Cavall.
claims.quote: tusk of Yskithyrwyn Penbaedd to shave myself withal, neither shall I profit by its use if it be not plucked alive out of his head.

claims.statement: In the Mabinogion pigs, especially boars, often trigger wars and raids; the Celts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mabinogion, babi dan babi jantan sering memicu perang dan penjarahan; bangsa Kelt.
claims.quote: Im walisischen Sagenkreis des Mabinogion sind Schweine, besonders Eber, oft der Auslöser für Kriege und Beutezüge.

claims.statement: Adar Rhiannon (birds of Rhiannon), three magical birds of the Mabinogi; wake the dead, lull the living; remote yet near; Britain.
claims.statement_id: Adar Rhiannon (burung-burung Rhiannon), tiga burung ajaib Mabinogi; membangunkan orang mati, menidurkan yang hidup; jauh tetapi tampak dekat; Britania.
claims.quote: the Adar Rhiannon ; "birds of Rhiannon", are specifically three magical birds, whose song can "wake the dead and lull the living to sleep". They also have a non-rational effect on space as they can be remote but seem very near.

claims.statement: Connected with Rhiannon, Queen of Dyfed, a British horse goddess; Welsh mythology.
claims.statement_id: Terkait Rhiannon, Ratu (Queen of) Dyfed, dewi kuda Britania (British); mitologi Welsh, Wales.
claims.quote: They are connected with Rhiannon the Queen of Dyfed who is thought to be a British euhemerized horse goddess, so part of Welsh mythology.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden Bencawr demanded them as Culhwch's task (Culhwch and Olwen); his last night of life.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr menuntutnya sebagai tugas Culhwch (Culhwch and Olwen); malam terakhir hidupnya.
claims.quote: The Adar Rhiannon were demanded by the giant Ysbaddaden Bencawr as a marriage task for Culhwch to complete. The giant wanted the Birds to soothe him as he faced his last night of life, prophesied as the consequence of his daughter's wedding.

claims.statement: Branwen ferch Llŷr: seven survivors feast at Harlech seven years; war with Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Branwen ferch Llŷr: tujuh penyintas berpesta di Harlech tujuh tahun; perang dengan Irlandia.
claims.quote: Before setting off, the Seven Survivors feast at Harlech for seven enchanted years, regaled by the three Birds of Rhiannon.

claims.statement: Lady Guest translation: seven years feasting at Harlech with the birds of Rhiannon singing.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Lady Guest: tujuh tahun berpesta di Harlech diiringi nyanyian burung Rhiannon.
claims.quote: In Harlech you will be feasting seven years, the birds of Rhiannon singing unto you the while.

claims.statement: The birds seemed far over the sea yet distinct as if close.
claims.statement_id: Burung tampak jauh di atas laut tetapi jelas seolah dekat.
claims.quote: and the birds seemed to them to be at a great distance from them over the sea, yet they appeared as distinct as if they were close by

claims.statement: Adhene, fairies of Manx tradition, Isle of Man; Cloan ny moyrn (Children of Pride); fallen angels.
claims.statement_id: Adhene, peri tradisi Manx, Pulau Man; Cloan ny moyrn (Anak-anak Kesombongan, Children of Pride); malaikat jatuh.
claims.quote: In Manx tradition, fairies were called Adhene and known as Cloan ny moyrn , which means the Children of Pride/Ambition, because they were regarded as having been fallen angels cast from heaven but too good for hell.

claims.statement: Sometimes kind, mostly mischievous; take babies or wives; powerless over errands of mercy.
claims.statement_id: Kadang baik, umumnya nakal; mengambil bayi atau istri; tak berdaya atas tugas belas kasih.
claims.quote: They could be benevolent but were mostly mischievous in association with humans, taking babies or wives when they wished, although it was believed that their powers were not effective over any human on an errand of mercy.

claims.statement: Child-sized; fish, herd cattle on hills; barrel-making in caves foretells good harvests.
claims.statement_id: Seukuran anak kecil; memancing, menggembala di bukit; membuat tong di gua pertanda panen baik.
claims.quote: About the size of a small child when visible, they fished at sea and herded their cattle on the hills. The Manx people knew there would be good fishing or harvests when they heard the fairies making storage barrels in the caves.

claims.statement: According to Moore, some Manx fairies are benevolent, curing men of diseases and delivering them from misfortune, while others are malevolent, stealing children, even abducting grown people, and bringing misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Moore, sebagian peri Manx baik hati, menyembuhkan penyakit dan melepaskan orang dari kemalangan, sedangkan yang lain jahat, mencuri anak, bahkan menculik orang dewasa, dan mendatangkan kemalangan.
claims.quote: Some of them are benevolent, curing men of diseases and delivering them from misfortune. Others are malevolent, stealing children, even abducting grown people, and bringing misfortune.

claims.statement: Moore writes that they are partly human and partly spiritual in nature and are visible to men only when they choose.
claims.statement_id: Moore menulis bahwa peri-peri itu sebagian manusiawi dan sebagian rohani dalam wataknya, dan hanya tampak oleh manusia bila mereka mau.
claims.quote: They are partly human and partly spiritual in their nature, and are visible to men only when they choose.

claims.statement: Moore says they are called 'the little people' or 'the good people', the word Fairy never being mentioned because they are supposed not to like it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Moore, mereka disebut "orang-orang kecil" atau "orang-orang baik", dan kata Fairy tidak pernah disebut karena dianggap tidak mereka sukai.
claims.quote: they are called “the little people”, or “the good people”, the word Fairy being never mentioned, as they are supposed not to like it.

claims.statement: According to Moore, they live in green hill sides, especially favouring the ancient tumuli.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Moore, mereka tinggal di lereng bukit hijau, terutama menyukai gundukan makam kuno.
claims.quote: They live in green hill sides, more especially affecting the ancient tumuli.

claims.statement: Ascapart (Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard), giant of English folklore conquered by Bevis of Hampton; carried Bevis, wife, horse.
claims.statement_id: Ascapart (Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard), raksasa folklor Inggris (English), ditaklukkan Bevis dari (of) Hampton; mengepit Bevis, istri, kuda.
claims.quote: In English folklore, Ascapart (also spelled Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart and Asgapard) was a legendary giant supposedly conquered by Bevis of Hampton, so huge as to carry Bevis, his wife, and horse under his arm.

claims.statement: 30 feet, smallest of his land; tree club stuck; Sir Bevis made him squire.
claims.statement_id: 30 kaki, terkecil di negerinya; gada pohon tertancap; Sir Bevis menjadikannya pengawal.
claims.quote: He was 30 feet tall but the smallest of his land, and was defeated after his club (made from a whole tree) was swung at Sir Bevis and became stuck in soft ground. Rather than slaying the giant however, Sir Bevis decided to make him his Squire.

claims.statement: Betrayed Bevis, took Josiane; killed by Bevis's friends.
claims.statement_id: Mengkhianati Bevis, membawa Josiane; dibunuh sahabat Bevis.
claims.quote: Later Ascapart betrayed Bevis and took his wife Josiane, who was imprisoned with Ascapart as her jailer. For this Ascapart was killed by Bevis' friends when they freed Josiane.

claims.statement: Buried under Bevis Mount or became part of the South Downs.
claims.statement_id: Dikubur di Bevis Mount atau menjadi bagian South Downs.
claims.quote: Ascapart was supposedly buried under Bevis Mount, or his body became a part of the South Downs when he fell.

claims.statement: Folklore of Hampshire and the New Forest; painted panels of Sir Bevis and Ascupart in the Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.
claims.statement_id: Folklor Hampshire dan New Forest; panel lukisan Sir Bevis dan Ascupart di Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.
claims.quote: Alongside the story of Bevis of Hampton, the giant appears in the local folklore of Hampshire and the New Forest; large medieval painted oak panels of Sir Bevis and Ascupart can be found in the Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery

claims.statement: According to the South Downs National Park page, Ascapart was small compared with the giants of his day and stood a mere 30 feet tall.
claims.statement_id: Menurut halaman Taman Nasional South Downs, Ascapart tergolong kecil dibanding raksasa-raksasa zamannya dan tingginya hanya sekitar 30 kaki.
claims.quote: Ascapart was a small giants compared to those of his day and stood a mere 30 foot tall.

claims.statement: The same page says Ascapart was more than capable of terrifying the local villages around Southampton.
claims.statement_id: Halaman yang sama menyebut Ascapart sangat mampu menakut-nakuti desa-desa di sekitar Southampton.
claims.quote: Nevertheless, Ascapart was more than capable of terrifying the local villages around Southampton.

claims.statement: Some say Ascapart lived only because Josain, Bevis's wife, persuaded Bevis to spare his life.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian penutur, Ascapart tetap hidup hanya karena Josain, istri Bevis, membujuk Bevis agar mengampuni nyawanya.
claims.quote: The only reason Ascapart lived, some say, was because Josain, Bevis’ wife persuaded Bevis to spare Ascapart’s life.

claims.statement: Some records recall that Ascapart did betray Bevis and kidnapped his wife, holding her prisoner; for that he met his death at the hands of Bevis's supporters, and where he fell his body became part of the Downs.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa catatan menyebut Ascapart memang mengkhianati Bevis dan menculik istrinya, menahannya; karena itu ia tewas di tangan para pendukung Bevis, dan di tempat ia jatuh tubuhnya menjadi bagian dari Downs.
claims.quote: In a twist to the tale, some records recall that Ascapart did indeed betray Bevis and kidnapped Bevis’ wife holding her prisoner. For that Ascapart met his death at the hands of Bevis’ supporters and where he fell, his body became a part of the Downs.

claims.statement: Bánánach, preternatural beings of early Irish folklore, battlefield spectres; with the bócanach, geniti glinne, demna aeóir in the Táin Bó Cúalnge.
claims.statement_id: Bánánach, makhluk gaib folklor Irlandia (Irish) awal, hantu medan perang; bersama bócanach, geniti glinne, demna aeóir dalam Táin Bó Cúalnge.
claims.quote: In early Irish folklore, the bánánach (Irish: [ˈbˠaːnˠaːnˠax], English: /ˈbɑːn.ɑːn.əx/) were preternatural beings, described as spectres which haunted battlefields.

claims.statement: Sent by the Tuatha Dé Danann to terrify Cú Chulainn's enemies.
claims.statement_id: Dikirim Tuatha Dé Danann menakuti musuh Cú Chulainn.
claims.quote: In the Táin Bó Cúalnge, the bánánach, bócanach, and geniti glinne are sent by the Tuatha Dé Danann strike fear into Cú Chulainn's enimies, answering to his battle cry.

claims.statement: Personify battle sounds; warded off by the Dond Cúalnge.
claims.statement_id: Personifikasi bunyi pertempuran; ditangkal Dond Cúalnge.
claims.quote: They are linked with (and sometimes considered personifications of) the sounds of battle, being used as a way to describe the sound of weapons clashing. All three of these beings are warded off by the Dond Cúalnge, a legendary bull mentioned in the Táin Bó Cúalnge.

claims.statement: In Faraday's translation of the Táin Bó Cúailnge, when the hero uttered his shout, goblins, sprites, spectres of the glen and demons of the air answered for terror of the shout.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Faraday atas Táin Bó Cúailnge, ketika sang pahlawan menyerukan teriakannya, goblin, sprite, hantu lembah, dan iblis udara menjawab karena ngeri akan teriakan itu.
claims.quote: and he uttered his hero's shout from his throat, so that goblins and sprites and spectres of the glen and demons of the air answered, for the terror of the shout which they uttered on high.

claims.statement: The same translation says goblins, sprites, ghosts of the glen and demons of the air cried from something he wore, before, above and around him, wherever he went before shedding the blood of warriors and enemies.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan yang sama menyebut goblin, sprite, hantu lembah, dan iblis udara berseru dari benda yang dikenakan sang pahlawan, di depan, di atas, dan di sekelilingnya, ke mana pun ia pergi sebelum menumpahkan darah para prajurit dan musuh.
claims.quote: For there used to cry from it equally goblins and sprites and ghosts of the glen and demons of the air, before and above and around, wherever he used to go before shedding the blood of warriors and enemies.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that the bánánach are mentioned alongside the bócanach ('goat-like battle spectre'), the geniti glinne ('female battle-spectre of the glen') and the demna aeóir ('demons of the air') in the Táin Bó Cúailnge.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bánánach disebut bersama bócanach ("hantu perang mirip kambing"), geniti glinne ("hantu perang perempuan dari lembah"), dan demna aeóir ("setan udara") dalam Táin Bó Cúailnge.
claims.quote: They are mentioned alongside the bócanach, ... "goat-like battle spectre") the geniti glinne ... "female battle-spectre of the glen") , and the demna aeóir ... ,"demons of the air") in the Táin Bó Cúalnge.

claims.statement: Bwystfil Bont (Beast of Bont), a legendary or imagined beast attacking livestock in Ceredigion, Wales; a giant black cat at dusk.
claims.statement_id: Bwystfil Bont (Beast of Bont), binatang legenda atau khayalan, menyerang ternak di Ceredigion, Wales; kucing hitam raksasa saat senja.
claims.quote: Bwystfil - chwedlonol neu ddychmygol yn ôl rhai - yw Bwystfil Bont sy’n parhau i ymosod ar anifeiliaid ffermydd Ceredigion.  Honnir gan nifer o lygad-dystion iddynt adnabod ffigur cath ddu enfawr ar hyd caeau ffermydd Sir Ceredigion wrth iddi nosi.

claims.statement: For 30 years police received reports of big cats like puma, panther, leopard, lynx; claw marks on sheep.
claims.statement_id: Selama 30 tahun polisi menerima laporan kucing besar mirip puma, panter, macan tutul, lynx; bekas cakaran pada domba.
claims.quote: Ers 30 mlynedd mae’r heddlu wedi derbyn galwadau niferus yn son am olwg o gathod enfawr tebyg i bwma, panther, llewpard neu lyncs.

claims.statement: An American, Tom Brown, came to Wales to investigate the Bwystfil.

claims.statement: A sheep's shoulder and leg torn off, the rest of the flock slept on.

claims.quote: Fodd bynnag, parhau i gysgu oedd gweddill y praidd.

claims.statement: According to the Cambrian News, in June 1981 twelve sheep were slaughtered by an unknown creature in the tiny village of Pontrhydfendigaid, known locally as Bont, west of the Cambrian Mountains range stretching across Ceredigion and Powys.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cambrian News, pada Juni 1981 dua belas domba disembelih oleh makhluk tak dikenal di desa kecil Pontrhydfendigaid, yang di daerah itu disebut Bont, di sebelah barat Pegunungan Cambrian yang membentang melintasi Ceredigion dan Powys.
claims.quote: In June 1981, 12 sheep were slaughtered by an unknown creature in the tiny village of Pontrhydfendigaid - known locally as Bont - which sits to the west of the Cambrian Mountains range stretching across Ceredigion and Powys.

claims.statement: Veterinarians from the UK Ministry of Agriculture, as it was then, are said to have concluded that whatever had killed the livestock must have been a 'great deal more powerful than a fox or a dog'.

claims.quote: Veterinarians from the UK Ministry of Agriculture, as it was then, are said to have released findings that whatever had killed the livestock must have been a ‘great deal more powerful than a fox or a dog’.

claims.statement: Biast Bhealach Odail (Biasd Bhealach Odail), monster or spirit of Scottish folklore, Odal Pass, Isle of Skye.

claims.quote: In Scottish folklore the Biast Bhealach Odail (older spelling: Biasd Bhealach Odail)is a monster or spirit that haunts Odal Pass on the Isle of Skye in Scotland.

claims.statement: Campbell (1902): sometimes the form of a man, a man with only one leg, a greyhound or beast prowling about; shrieks; at night.
claims.statement_id: John Gregorson Campbell (1902): kadang berwujud lelaki (form of a man), lelaki berkaki satu (one leg), greyhound atau binatang berkeliaran (beast prowling); menjerit; malam hari.
claims.quote: Sometimes it bore the form of a man, sometimes of a man with only one leg. At other times it appeared like a greyhound or beast prowling about

claims.statement: A victim dead with two wounds, side and leg; night travellers attacked.
claims.statement_id: Korban tewas dengan dua luka di sisi dan kaki; pelancong diserang malam hari.
claims.quote: One of its victims, according to legend, was found dead on the roadside pierced with two wounds, one on his side and one on his leg with a hand pressed on each wound.

claims.statement: Attacks ceased; Katharine Briggs: ghost of a murdered man seeking revenge; Campbell.
claims.statement_id: Serangan berhenti; Katharine Briggs: hantu orang dibunuh yang mencari balas dendam; Campbell.
claims.quote: He further mentions that the attacks ceased after the victim's body was found, which led the folklorist Katharine Briggs to suggest that the monster may have been the ghost of a murdered man looking for revenge.

claims.statement: Campbell writes that at the time the road was being made, the Pass was haunted by 'something' awful, the more awful because its character was not distinctly known.
claims.statement_id: Campbell menulis bahwa pada saat jalan dibangun, celah itu dihantui "sesuatu" yang mengerikan, terlebih karena sifatnya tidak diketahui dengan jelas.
claims.quote: At the time it was being made, the Pass was haunted by " something " awful — the more awful that its character was not distinctly known

claims.statement: According to Campbell, travellers through the Pass at night were often thrown down and hurt by it and with difficulty made their way to a place of safety.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Campbell, para pelancong yang melewati celah itu pada malam hari sering dilempar jatuh dan terluka olehnya, lalu dengan susah payah mencapai tempat aman.
claims.quote: Travellers through the Pass at night were often thrown down and hurt by it, and with difficulty made their way to a place of safety.

claims.statement: Campbell records that it ceased when a man was found dead at the roadside, pierced with two wounds.
