claims.quote: It ceased when a man was found dead at the roadside, pierced with two wounds

claims.statement: Brag, a shapeshifting goblin of Northumbrian folklore (Northumberland, Durham); horse or donkey; bucks riders into ponds.
claims.statement_id: Brag, goblin pengubah wujud folklor Northumbria (Northumberland, Durham); kuda atau keledai; melempar penunggang ke kolam.
claims.quote: A brag is a mischievous shapeshifting goblin in the folklore of Northumbria (Northumberland and Durham) and often takes the form of a horse or donkey. It is fond of letting unsuspecting humans ride on its back before bucking them off into a pond or bush and running away laughing.

claims.statement: Picktree Brag: calf with white handkerchief, headless man, four men with a white sheet.
claims.statement_id: Picktree Brag: anak sapi berselendang putih, lelaki tanpa kepala, empat orang dengan kain putih.
claims.quote: One notable example is the Picktree Brag that was said to take other unusual forms such as a calf with a white handkerchief around its neck, a naked headless man, and even four men holding a white sheet.

claims.statement: The Humbleknowe brag unseen, hideous noises at night.
claims.statement_id: Brag Humbleknowe tak terlihat, bunyi mengerikan malam hari.
claims.quote: A brag at Humbleknowe was never seen but made hideous noises in the night.

claims.statement: According to Henderson, the Picktree Brag also appeared as a 'dick-ass', as four men holding up a white sheet, or as a naked man without a head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, Picktree Brag juga pernah tampil sebagai "dick-ass" (keledai), sebagai empat orang yang mengangkat selembar kain putih, atau sebagai lelaki telanjang tanpa kepala.
claims.quote: Again it appeared as a " dick-ass," as four men holding up a white sheet, or as a naked man without a head.

claims.statement: In the tale Henderson records, a bold man returning from a christening met the Brag and leapt upon its back.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Henderson, seorang lelaki pemberani yang pulang dari pembaptisan bertemu Brag dan melompat ke punggungnya.
claims.quote: Once, in that very suit, returning from a christening, he encountered the Brag, and being a bold man, he leapt upon its back

claims.statement: In the same tale, at last the Brag threw him into the middle of the pond and ran away, setting up a great nicker and laugh, just like a Christian.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang sama, pada akhirnya Brag melemparkannya ke tengah kolam dan lari sambil meringkik dan tertawa seperti orang Kristen.
claims.quote: at last it threw him into the middle o' the pond, and ran away, setting up a great nicker and laugh, just for all the world like a Christian.

claims.statement: Brown Man of the Muirs, a dwarf of Anglo-Scottish border folklore, guardian spirit of wild animals.
claims.statement_id: Brown Man of the Muirs, kurcaci folklor perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish), roh pelindung hewan liar.
claims.quote: In the folklore on the Anglo-Scottish border, the Brown Man of the Muirs is a dwarf who serves as a guardian spirit of wild animals.

claims.statement: William Henderson, Folklore of the Northern Counties (1879); Robert Surtees, Sir Walter Scott; Great Rebellion; Newcastle; Elsdon; strong dwarf, brown dress, red hair, bull's eyes.
claims.statement_id: William Henderson, Folklore of the Northern Counties (1879); Robert Surtees, Sir Walter Scott; Pemberontakan Besar (Great Rebellion); Newcastle; Elsdon; kurcaci kuat, berbaju cokelat, rambut merah, mata banteng.
claims.quote: the "Brown man of the Muirs", a dwarf very strong and stoutly built, his dress brown like withered bracken, his head covered with frizzled red hair, his countenance ferocious, and his eyes glowing like those of a bull.

claims.statement: Rebuked the hunter; eats berries, nuts, apples; invited him home.
claims.statement_id: Menegur pemburu; makan beri, kacang, apel; mengundangnya pulang.
claims.quote: the stranger reproved the hunter for trespassing on his demesnes and slaying the creatures who were his subjects, and informed him how he himself lived only on whortleberries, nuts, and apples, he invited him home.

claims.statement: Would have been torn apart if he crossed; died within the year.
claims.statement_id: Bila menyeberang akan dicabik; meninggal dalam setahun.
claims.quote: It was thought that had the young man crossed the water the dwarf would have torn him to pieces. As it was he died within the year

claims.statement: Walter Scott: related to the duergar of Northumberland.
claims.statement_id: Walter Scott: berkerabat dengan duergar Northumberland.
claims.quote: Walter Scott in a return letter to Surtees suggested that the Brown Man may be related to the duergar (dwarfs) of Northumberland.

claims.statement: Henderson says the Brown Man of the Muirs tale comes from a letter from Surtees to Sir W. Scott, given in the memoir in vol. iv of Surtees's History of Durham, on the authority of an old dame named Elizabeth Cockburn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, kisah Brown Man of the Muirs dimuat dalam surat Surtees kepada Sir W. Scott, yang tercantum dalam memoar di jilid keempat History of Durham karya Surtees, dan disampaikan atas keterangan seorang perempuan tua bernama Elizabeth Cockburn.
claims.quote: In a letter from Mr. Surtees to Sir W. Scott, given in the memoir prefixed to vol. iv. of Surtees's History of Durham, we read, on the authority of an old dame named Elizabeth Cockburn

claims.statement: Henderson presents the Brown Man of the Muirs as a mysterious denizen of the wild moorlands, set beside the attendant sprites of Scottish homesteads.
claims.statement_id: Henderson menempatkan Brown Man of the Muirs sebagai penghuni misterius padang rawa liar, berpasangan dengan roh-roh pendamping rumah-rumah pertanian Skotlandia.
claims.quote: If the Scottish homesteads have their attendant sprites, the wild moorlands are not without their mysterious denizens.

claims.statement: In folklore the Brown Man appears as a solitary fairy, but in fairy tale literature he is a member of a tribe of similar beings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor Brown Man muncul sebagai peri penyendiri, tetapi dalam sastra dongeng ia anggota suku makhluk serupa.
claims.quote: In folklore the Brown Man appears as a solitary fairy, but in fairy tale literature he is a member of a tribe of similar beings.

claims.statement: Bucca (Bocka, bockas), a male sea-spirit of Cornish folklore, a merman, a hobgoblin in storms; related to the Irish Púca, Welsh Pwca, Breton mari-morgans.
claims.statement_id: Bucca (Bocka, bockas), roh laut lelaki folklor Cornwall (Cornish), manusia ikan, hobgoblin saat badai; berkerabat Púca Irlandia (Irish), Pwca Welsh, mari-morgan Breton.
claims.quote: is a male sea-spirit in Cornish folklore, a merman, that inhabited mines and coastal communities as a hobgoblin during storms. The mythological creature is a type of water spirit likely related to the Púca from Irish, the Pwca from Welsh folklore, and the female mari-morgans

claims.statement: Rev W. S. Lach-Szyrma: possibly a pagan sea god like the Irish Nechtan or British Nodens.
claims.statement_id: Pendeta (Rev) W. S. Lach-Szyrma: mungkin dewa laut pagan seperti Nechtan Irlandia (Irish) atau Nodens Britania (British).
claims.quote: Rev W. S. Lach-Szyrma, one 19th-century writer on Cornish antiquities, suggested the Bucca had originally been an ancient pagan deity of the sea such as Irish Nechtan or British Nodens

claims.statement: Mentioned in Gwreans an bys (1611).
claims.statement_id: Disebut dalam Gwreans an bys (1611).
claims.quote: In 1611, in the Cornish language book Gwreans an bys known in English as The Creation of the World the Bucca is mentioned

claims.statement: William Bottrell (1890): Bucka Gwidden (good), Bucka Dhu (evil); Newlyn and Mousehole fishermen left catch for Bucka.
claims.statement_id: William Bottrell (1890): Bucka Gwidden (baik), Bucka Dhu (jahat); nelayan Newlyn dan Mousehole meninggalkan tangkapan untuk Bucka.
claims.quote: I have been told, by persons of credit, that within the last forty years it was a usual practice with Newlyn and Mousehole fishermen to leave on the sand at night a portion of their catch for Bucka.

claims.statement: Bucca Widn (white) and Bucca Dhu (black); Penzance: south-westerly storms called Bucca calling.
claims.statement_id: Bucca Widn (putih) dan Bucca Dhu (hitam); Penzance: badai barat daya disebut Bucca calling.
claims.quote: Bucca also seems to associated with the wind, in Penzance it was customary to refer to storms that emanated from a southwesterly direction as "Bucca calling"; sailors and fishermen also believe that Bucca's voice carried on the wind.

claims.statement: Robert Hunt writes that the Buccas or Knockers are the sprites of the mines and correspond to the Kobals of the German mines, the Duergars and the Trolls.

claims.quote: These are the sprites of the mines, and correspond to the Kobals of the German mines, the Duergars, and the Trolls.

claims.statement: According to Hunt, the buccas or knockers are believed to inhabit the rocks, caves, adits and wells of Cornwall.

claims.quote: THE buccas or knockers are believed to inhabit the rocks, caves, adits, and wells of Cornwall.

claims.quote: Dando's Dogs also known as the Devil's Dandy Dogs, are mythical creatures in English folklore. They are hounds that take part in the Wild Hunt. They are associated with Black Dogs, as a generic term for canine apparitions.

claims.statement: Dando, a sinful priest and able huntsman; drinks after a Sunday hunt.

claims.quote: In both versions, the huntsman whisks Dando away to Hell, while Dando's dogs give futile chase. It is said that on early Sunday mornings, "Dando's Dogs" can be heard, either pursuing game or searching for Dando.

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: duplikat/alias dari water-bull: artikel de Der Elfstier (juga Wasserstier, Irlandia/Skotlandia tarbh uisge, Manx tarroo ushtey) membahas banteng air dari folklor Irlandia, Skotlandia dan Pulau Man yang sudah ada di data sebagai water-bull.
